translations.idiomatic: Slandered by the eunuch bureau, he was demoted to Right Regular Attendant with provisional charge of the Ministry of the Civil Office and its selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，德裕罷相，出仲郢爲鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu was removed as chancellor and Zhong Ying was sent out as Prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu was removed as chancellor and Zhong Ying was sent out as Prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 周墀自江西移鎭滑臺。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi was transferred from Jiangxi to govern Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi was transferred from Jiangxi to govern Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 過鄭，觀其境内大理，甚獎之。

translations.literal: Passing through Zheng, he observed how well governed the territory was and greatly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Zheng, he observed how well governed the territory was and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 俄而墀入輔政，遷爲河南尹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chi entered the government as chief minister, and Zhong Ying was transferred to metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chi entered the government as chief minister, and Zhong Ying was transferred to Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 蒞事逾月，召拜戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month in office, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month in office, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 居無何，墀罷知政事。

translations.literal: Before long Chi was removed from active government.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chi was removed from active government.

sentences.zh: 同列有疑仲郢與墀善，左授秘書監。

translations.literal: Colleagues suspected Zhong Ying's closeness to Chi, and he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues suspected Zhong Ying's closeness to Chi, and he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 數月，復出爲河南尹。

translations.literal: Several months later he was again sent out as metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was again sent out as Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 以寬惠爲政，言事者以爲不類京兆之政。

translations.literal: He governed with lenience and kindness, and memorialists said this did not resemble his metropolitan policy.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with lenience and kindness, and critics said this did not resemble his metropolitan policy.

sentences.zh: 仲郢曰：「輦轂之下，彈壓爲先；

translations.literal: Zhong Ying said: "Beneath the imperial carriage, suppression comes first;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying said, "Beneath the imperial carriage, suppression comes first;

sentences.zh: 郡邑之治，惠養爲本。

translations.literal: in governing prefectures and districts, nourishing the people is fundamental.
translations.idiomatic: in governing prefectures and districts, nourishing the people is fundamental.

sentences.zh: 何取類耶？」

translations.literal: Why should they be alike?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should they be alike?"

sentences.zh: 大中年，轉梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he was transferred to Prefect of Zi and Military Governor of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he was transferred to Prefect of Zi and Military Governor of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 孔目吏邊章簡者，以貨交近幸，前後廉使無如之何。

translations.literal: The chief clerk Bian Zhangjian used wealth to cultivate connections with those close to the throne; successive inspection commissioners could do nothing about him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk Bian Zhangjian used wealth to cultivate connections with those close to the throne; successive inspection commissioners could do nothing about him.

sentences.zh: 仲郢因事決殺，部内肅然，不俟行法而自理。

translations.literal: Zhong Ying seized on an offense and had him executed; within his jurisdiction all was solemn, and order was restored without waiting for the law to be formally applied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying seized on an offense and had him executed; within his jurisdiction all was solemn, and order was restored without waiting for formal legal process.

sentences.zh: 在鎭五年，美績流聞，征爲吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After five years in the post his fine achievements spread abroad, and he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in the post his fine achievements spread abroad, and he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 入朝未謝，改兵部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Before he had thanked the throne on entering court, he was changed to Vice Minister of War and made Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could thank the throne on entering court, he was changed to Vice Minister of War and made Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 大中十二年，罷使，守刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dazhong he was relieved of the commission and remained Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dazhong he was relieved of the commission and remained Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，轉兵部，加金紫光祿大夫、河東男、食邑三百戸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to the Ministry of War, with the added titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Baron of Hedong, and a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to the Ministry of War, with the added titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Baron of Hedong, and a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 俄出爲興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Xingyuan and Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Governor of Xingyuan and Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鳳州刺史盧方乂以輕罪決部叫，數日而斃。

translations.literal: Lu Fangyi, Prefect of Feng, punished a subordinate with a light offense by having him shout; several days later the man died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fangyi, Prefect of Feng, punished a subordinate for a minor offense by having him shout under discipline; several days later the man died.

sentences.zh: 其妻列訴，又旁引他吏，械系滿獄。

translations.literal: His wife filed a complaint and also implicated other officials; prisoners in shackles filled the jail.
translations.idiomatic: His wife filed a complaint and also implicated other officials; prisoners in shackles filled the jail.

sentences.zh: 仲郢召其妻謂之曰：「刺史科小罪誡人，但本非死刑，雖未出辜，其實病死。」

translations.literal: Zhong Ying summoned the wife and told her: "The prefect punished a minor offense to admonish the man; it was never a capital crime. Though he had not yet completed his term of guilt, in fact he died of illness."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying summoned the wife and told her, "The prefect punished a minor offense to admonish the man; it was never a capital crime. Though he had not yet completed his term of guilt, in fact he died of illness."

sentences.zh: 罰方乂百直，系者皆釋，郡人深感之。

translations.literal: He fined Fangyi one hundred strings of cash; all those imprisoned were released, and the people of the prefecture were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: He fined Fangyi one hundred strings of cash; all those imprisoned were released, and the people of the prefecture were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 因決贓吏過當，以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: Because he punished corrupt officials excessively, he was made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because he punished corrupt officials excessively, he was made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 逾年，爲虢州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he became Prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he became Prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 數月，檢校尚書左僕射、東都留守。

translations.literal: Several months later he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Garrison Commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 盜發先人墓，棄官歸華原。

translations.literal: When robbers opened the tombs of his ancestors, he resigned his office and returned to Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers desecrated his ancestors' tombs, he resigned his office and returned to Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 除華州刺史，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Hua but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Hua but declined.

sentences.zh: 數月，以本官爲鄆州刺史，天平軍節度觀察等使，授節鉞於華原別墅，卒於鎭。

translations.literal: Several months later, with his former rank he became Prefect of Yan, Military Governor and Inspector of the Tianping Army and other posts; the command baton was conferred at his villa in Huayuan, and he died in the post.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, retaining his former rank, he became Prefect of Yan, Military Governor and Inspector of the Tianping Army; the command baton was conferred at his villa in Huayuan, and he died in the post.

sentences.zh: 初，仲郢自拜諫議後，毎遷官，群烏大集於升平裏第，廷樹戟架皆滿，凡五日而散。

translations.literal: At first, from the time Zhong Ying was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance, every time he was promoted flocks of crows gathered in great numbers at his mansion in Shengping Lane, filling the courtyard trees and halberd racks; after five days they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Zhong Ying was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance, every promotion brought flocks of crows in great numbers to his mansion in Shengping Lane, filling the courtyard trees and halberd racks; after five days they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 詔下，不復集，家人以爲候，唯除天平，烏不集。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued they did not gather again; his family took this as an omen—only for the Tianping appointment did the crows not gather.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued the crows did not gather again; his family took this as an omen—only for the Tianping appointment did the crows stay away.

sentences.zh: 仲郢嚴禮法，重氣義，嘗感李德裕之知。

translations.literal: Zhong Ying was strict in ritual propriety and valued integrity; he had once been moved by Li Deyu's recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying was strict in ritual propriety and valued integrity; he had long been moved by Li Deyu's recognition.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，李氏無祿仕者。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong court no member of the Li clan held salaried office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong court no member of the Li clan held salaried office.

sentences.zh: 仲郢領鹽鐵時，取德裕兄子從質爲推官，知蘇州院事，令以祿利贍南宅。

translations.literal: When Zhong Ying headed the Salt and Iron Commission, he took Deyu's elder brother's son Congzhi as a investigating officer in charge of the Suzhou office and ordered that his salary support the southern residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Ying headed the Salt and Iron Commission, he took Deyu's elder brother's son Congzhi as investigating officer in charge of the Suzhou office and ordered that his salary support the southern residence.

sentences.zh: 令孤綯爲宰相，頗不悅。

translations.literal: Linghu Tao became chancellor and was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Tao became chancellor, he was quite displeased.

sentences.zh: 仲郢與綯書自明，其要云：「任安不去，常自愧於昔人；

translations.literal: Zhong Ying wrote Tao a letter to explain himself; the gist ran: "Ren An did not leave, and I am constantly ashamed before the men of old;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying wrote Tao a letter to explain himself; the gist ran, "Ren An did not leave, and I am constantly ashamed before the men of old;

sentences.zh: 呉詠自裁，亦何施於今日？

translations.literal: Wu Yong took his own life—what use would that be today?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong took his own life—what use would that be today?

sentences.zh: 李太尉受責既久，其家已空，遂絶蒸嘗，誠增痛惻。」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Li has long borne punishment; his household is already empty and ancestral offerings have ceased—this truly adds to my anguish."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Li has long borne punishment; his household is already empty and ancestral offerings have ceased—this truly adds to my anguish."

sentences.zh: 綯深感嘆，尋與從質正員官。

translations.literal: Tao was deeply moved and sighing; soon afterward he gave Congzhi a regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was deeply moved; soon afterward he gave Congzhi a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 仲郢以禮法自持，私居未嘗不拱手，内齋未嘗不束帶。

translations.literal: Zhong Ying held himself to ritual propriety; at home he never failed to stand with hands clasped, and for inner fasts he never failed to wear his sash.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ying held himself to ritual propriety; at home he never failed to stand with hands clasped, and for private devotions he never failed to wear his sash.

sentences.zh: 三爲大鎭，廄無名馬，衣不薰香。

translations.literal: Though thrice governor of a great command, his stables held no famous horses and his robes were not scented.
translations.idiomatic: Though thrice governor of a great command, his stables held no famous horses and his robes bore no perfume.

sentences.zh: 退公布巻，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: When he retired he spread out books and did not put them away day or night.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired he spread out books and never put them away, day or night.

sentences.zh: 《九經》、《三史》一鈔；

translations.literal: The Nine Classics and the Three Histories he copied once;
translations.idiomatic: He copied the Nine Classics and the Three Histories once;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已來南北史再鈔；

translations.literal: the Northern and Southern Histories from Wei and Jin onward he copied twice;
translations.idiomatic: the Northern and Southern Histories from Wei and Jin onward he copied twice;

sentences.zh: 手鈔分門三十巻，號《柳氏自備》。

translations.literal: by hand he copied thirty fascicles arranged by category, titled "The Liu Family's Self-Sufficiency."
translations.idiomatic: by hand he copied thirty fascicles arranged by category, titled "The Liu Family's Self-Sufficiency."

sentences.zh: 又精釋典，《瑜伽》、《智度大論》皆再鈔；

translations.literal: He was also versed in Buddhist scriptures; the Yogacarabhumi and the Mahaprajnaparamita Sastra he copied twice;
translations.idiomatic: He was also versed in Buddhist scriptures; the Yogacarabhumi and the Mahaprajnaparamita Sastra he copied twice;

sentences.zh: 自余佛書，多手記要義。

translations.literal: of the remaining Buddhist books, he mostly noted the essentials by hand.
translations.idiomatic: of the remaining Buddhist books, he mostly noted the essentials by hand.

sentences.zh: 小楷精謹，無一字肆筆。

translations.literal: His small regular script was precise and careful, without a single careless stroke.
translations.idiomatic: His small regular script was precise and careful, without a single careless stroke.

sentences.zh: 撰《尚書二十四司箴》，韓愈、柳宗元深賞之。

translations.literal: He composed "Admonitions for the Twenty-Four Bureaus of the Book of Documents," which Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan deeply admired.
translations.idiomatic: He composed "Admonitions for the Twenty-Four Bureaus of the Book of Documents," which Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan deeply admired.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十巻。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子珪、璧、玭。

translations.literal: His sons were Gui, Bi, and Pin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gui, Bi, and Pin.

sentences.zh: 珪，字鎭方，大中五年登進士第，累辟使府，早卒。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Zhenfang, passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Dazhong, was repeatedly recruited to prefectural staffs, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Zhenfang, passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Dazhong, was repeatedly recruited to prefectural staffs, and died young.

sentences.zh: 璧，大中九年登進士第。

translations.literal: Bi passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Bi passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 文格髙雅。

translations.literal: His literary style was lofty and refined.
translations.idiomatic: His literary style was lofty and refined.

sentences.zh: 嘗爲《馬嵬詩》，詩人韓琮、李商隱嘉之。

translations.literal: He once wrote "Poem on Mawei," which the poets Han Cong and Li Shangyin praised.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote "Poem on Mawei," which the poets Han Cong and Li Shangyin praised.

sentences.zh: 馬植鎭陳許，辟爲掌書記，又從植汴州。

translations.literal: When Ma Zhi governed Chen and Xu, he recruited Bi as chief secretary; Bi later followed Zhi to Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Zhi governed Chen and Xu, he recruited Bi as chief secretary; Bi later followed Zhi to Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李瓚鎭桂管，奏爲觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Li Zan governed Guiguan, he recommended Bi as administrative aide to the inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zan governed Guiguan, he recommended Bi as administrative aide to the inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 軍政不愜，璧極言不納，拂衣而去。

translations.literal: Military and civil administration did not satisfy him; Bi spoke out to the limit and was not heeded, so he shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfied with military and civil administration, Bi spoke out to the limit and was not heeded, so he shook out his robes and left.

sentences.zh: 桂府尋亂，入爲右補闕。

translations.literal: The Guiguan headquarters soon fell into disorder; he entered service as Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Guiguan headquarters soon fell into disorder; he entered service as Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗幸蜀，召充翰林學士，累遷諫議大夫，充職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Bi was summoned as Hanlin Academician, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance, and continued in that office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Bi was summoned as Hanlin Academician, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance, and continued in that office.

sentences.zh: 玭應兩經舉，釋褐秘書正字。

translations.literal: Pin entered the Two Classics examination, and on leaving office became a proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pin entered the Two Classics examination and took his first post as proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又書判拔萃，髙湜辟爲度支推官。

translations.literal: He also excelled in the Document Judgment examination; Gao Shi recruited him as investigating officer in the Revenue Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He also excelled in the Document Judgment examination; Gao Shi recruited him as investigating officer in the Revenue Commission.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜右補闕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 湜出鎭澤潞，奏爲節度副使。

translations.literal: When Shi went out to govern Ze and Lu, he recommended Pin as deputy military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi went out to govern Ze and Lu, he recommended Pin as deputy military governor.

sentences.zh: 入爲殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered service as attendant palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as attendant palace censor.

sentences.zh: 李蔚鎭襄陽，辟爲掌書記。

translations.literal: When Li Wei governed Xiangyang, he recruited Pin as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wei governed Xiangyang, he recruited Pin as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 湜再鎭澤潞，復爲副使。

translations.literal: When Shi again governed Ze and Lu, Pin again served as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi again governed Ze and Lu, Pin again served as deputy.

sentences.zh: 入爲刑部員外。

translations.literal: He entered service as Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 湜爲亂將所逐，貶髙要尉，玭三上疎申理。

translations.literal: Shi was driven out by mutinous officers and demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao; Pin thrice submitted memorials in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was driven out by mutinous officers and demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao; Pin thrice submitted memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 湜見疎本嘆曰：「我自辨析，亦不及此。」

translations.literal: When Shi saw the memorial text he sighed: "Even my own analysis does not match this."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi saw the memorial text he sighed, "Even my own analysis does not match this."

sentences.zh: 尋出廣州節度副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as deputy military governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as deputy military governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，黃巣陷廣州，郡人鄧承勛以小舟載玭脱禍。

translations.literal: The next year Huang Chao captured Guangzhou; a townsman, Deng Chengxun, carried Pin in a small boat to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Huang Chao captured Guangzhou; a townsman, Deng Chengxun, carried Pin in a small boat to safety.

sentences.zh: 召爲起居郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Court Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Court Diarist.

sentences.zh: 賊陷長安，爲刃所傷，出奔行在，歴諫議給事中，位至御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the rebels captured Chang'an he was wounded by a blade; he fled to the mobile court, served through Grand Master of Remonstrance and Attendant of the Secretariat, and rose to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels captured Chang'an he was wounded by a blade; he fled to the mobile court, served through Grand Master of Remonstrance and Attendant of the Secretariat, and rose to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 玭嘗著書誡其子弟曰：

translations.literal: Pin once wrote a book admonishing his sons and younger brothers:
translations.idiomatic: Pin once wrote a book admonishing his sons and younger brothers:

sentences.zh: 予幼聞先訓，講論家法。

translations.literal: From childhood I heard the instructions of my forebears and discussions of our family rules.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood I heard the instructions of my forebears and discussions of our family rules.

sentences.zh: 立身以孝悌爲基，以恭默爲本，以畏怯爲務，以勤儉爲法，以交結爲末事，以氣義爲兇人。

translations.literal: Establish the person on filial piety and brotherly duty as foundation, on respectful silence as root, on cautious timidity as task, on diligence and frugality as method, on forming connections as a matter of last resort, and on swaggering righteousness as the way of violent men.
translations.idiomatic: Establish yourself on filial piety and brotherly duty as foundation, on respectful silence as root, on cautious timidity as duty, on diligence and frugality as method, on forming connections as a matter of last resort, and on swaggering righteousness as the mark of violent men.

sentences.zh: 肥家以忍順，保交以簡敬。

translations.literal: Enrich the household through forbearance and compliance; preserve friendships through simplicity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Enrich the household through forbearance and compliance; preserve friendships through simplicity and respect.

sentences.zh: 百行備，疑身之未周；

translations.literal: Though the hundred conduct-points are complete, one may still doubt whether the person is whole;
translations.idiomatic: Though the hundred conduct-points are complete, one may still doubt whether the person is whole;

sentences.zh: 三緘密，慮言之或失。

translations.literal: though the threefold seal is tight, one still fears that words may slip.
translations.idiomatic: though the threefold seal is tight, one still fears that words may slip.

sentences.zh: 廣記如不及，求名如儻來。

translations.literal: Record widely as though never enough; seek fame as though it came by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Record widely as though never enough; seek fame as though it came by chance.

sentences.zh: 去吝與驕，庶幾減過。

translations.literal: Cast off stinginess and arrogance, and one may perhaps reduce faults.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off stinginess and arrogance, and one may perhaps reduce one's faults.

sentences.zh: 蒞官則潔己省事，而後可以言守法；

translations.literal: In holding office, keep oneself pure and reduce affairs; only then may one speak of upholding the law;
translations.idiomatic: In holding office, keep yourself pure and reduce affairs; only then may one speak of upholding the law;

sentences.zh: 守法而後可以言養人。

translations.literal: only after upholding the law may one speak of nourishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: only after upholding the law may one speak of nourishing the people.

sentences.zh: 直不近禍，廉不沽名。

translations.literal: Uprightness does not court disaster; integrity does not trade for reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Uprightness does not court disaster; integrity does not trade for reputation.

sentences.zh: 廩祿雖微，不可易黎氓之膏血；

translations.literal: Though salary and grain are slight, one must not exchange them for the lifeblood of the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Though salary and grain are slight, one must not exchange them for the lifeblood of the common people;

sentences.zh: 榎楚雖用，不可恣褊狹之胸襟。

translations.literal: though the mulberry stick may be used, one must not indulge a narrow and petty breast.
translations.idiomatic: though the rod may be used, one must not indulge a narrow and petty breast.

sentences.zh: 憂與福不偕，潔與富不並。

translations.literal: Care and fortune do not go together; purity and wealth do not stand side by side.
translations.idiomatic: Care and fortune do not go together; purity and wealth do not stand side by side.

sentences.zh: 比見門家子孫，其先正直當官，耿介特立，不畏強禦；

translations.literal: I have lately seen descendants of our house whose forebears were upright in office, stern and independent, unafraid of the powerful;
translations.idiomatic: I have lately seen descendants of our house whose forebears were upright in office, stern and independent, unafraid of the powerful;

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，唯好犯上，更無他能。

translations.literal: when they declined, they only delighted in defying superiors and had no other ability.
translations.idiomatic: when they declined, they only delighted in defying superiors and had no other ability.

sentences.zh: 如其先遜順處己，和柔保身，以遠悔尤；

translations.literal: If their forebears were yielding in conduct, gentle in preserving themselves, and kept far from regret and blame;
translations.idiomatic: If their forebears were yielding in conduct, gentle in preserving themselves, and kept far from regret and blame;

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，但有暗劣，莫知所宗。

translations.literal: when they declined, they had only dull incapacity and knew nothing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: when they declined, they had only dull incapacity and knew nothing to follow.

sentences.zh: 此際幾微，非賢不達。

translations.literal: At this subtle turning point, only the worthy perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: At this subtle turning point, only the worthy perceive it.

sentences.zh: 夫壞名災己，辱先喪家。

translations.literal: To ruin one's name and bring disaster on oneself, disgrace one's ancestors and destroy the family—
translations.idiomatic: To ruin one's name and bring disaster on oneself, disgrace one's ancestors and destroy the family—

sentences.zh: 其失尤大者五，宜深志之。

translations.literal: the failures especially great number five; they should be deeply borne in mind.
translations.idiomatic: the failures especially great number five; they should be deeply borne in mind.

sentences.zh: 其一，自求安逸，靡甘淡泊，茍利於己，不恤人言。

translations.literal: The first: seeking ease for oneself, refusing to be content with simplicity, grasping profit for oneself without caring for others' words.
translations.idiomatic: The first: seeking ease for oneself, refusing to be content with simplicity, grasping profit for oneself without caring for others' words.

sentences.zh: 其二，不知儒術，不悅古道：懵前經而不恥，論當世而解頤；

translations.literal: The second: not knowing Confucian learning, not delighting in the ancient way—befuddled by the former classics yet unashamed, discussing the present age with grinning ease;
translations.idiomatic: The second: not knowing Confucian learning, not delighting in the ancient way—befuddled by the former classics yet unashamed, discussing the present age with grinning ease;

sentences.zh: 身既寡知，惡人有學。

translations.literal: the person himself has little knowledge, yet hates those who have learning.
translations.idiomatic: the person himself has little knowledge, yet hates those who have learning.

sentences.zh: 其三，勝己者厭之，佞己者悅之，唯樂戲譚，莫思古道。

translations.literal: The third: detesting those who surpass oneself, delighting in those who flatter oneself, taking pleasure only in jest and talk, never thinking of the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: The third: detesting those who surpass oneself, delighting in those who flatter oneself, taking pleasure only in jest and talk, never thinking of the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 聞人之善嫉之，聞人之惡揚之。

translations.literal: On hearing others' good one is jealous; on hearing others' evil one spreads it.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing others' good one is jealous; on hearing others' evil one spreads it.

sentences.zh: 浸漬頗僻，銷刻德義，簪裾徒在，廝養何殊。

translations.literal: Soaked in perversity, moral principle is filed away; though the cap and gown remain, what difference from a groom?
translations.idiomatic: Soaked in perversity, moral principle is filed away; though the cap and gown remain, what difference from a groom?

sentences.zh: 其四，崇好慢遊，耽嗜曲糵，以銜杯爲髙致，以勤事爲俗流，習之易荒，覺已難悔。

translations.literal: The fourth: loving idle wandering, addicted to wine—taking the raised cup as lofty attainment and diligent service as vulgar fashion; the habit is easy to waste away, and once aware it is hard to repent.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: loving idle wandering, addicted to wine—taking the raised cup as lofty attainment and diligent service as vulgar fashion; the habit is easy to waste away, and once aware it is hard to repent.

sentences.zh: 其五，急於名宦，昵近權要，一資半級，雖或得之；

translations.literal: The fifth: urgent for rank and office, drawing close to the powerful; one salary or half a grade may sometimes be obtained,
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: urgent for rank and office, drawing close to the powerful; one salary or half a grade may sometimes be obtained,

sentences.zh: 衆怒群猜，鮮有存者。

translations.literal: but popular anger and collective suspicion—few survive.
translations.idiomatic: but popular anger and collective suspicion—few survive.

sentences.zh: 茲五不是，甚於痤疽。

translations.literal: These five wrongs are worse than boils.
translations.idiomatic: These five wrongs are worse than boils.

sentences.zh: 痤疽則砭石可瘳，五失則巫醫莫及。

translations.literal: Boils may be cured with stone needles; the five failures are beyond shaman and physician.
translations.idiomatic: Boils may be cured with stone needles; the five failures are beyond shaman and physician.

sentences.zh: 前賢炯戒，方冊具存，近代覆車，聞見相接。

translations.literal: The bright warnings of former worthies are fully preserved in the records; overturned carts of recent times are heard and seen in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The bright warnings of former worthies are fully preserved in the records; overturned carts of recent times are heard and seen in succession.

sentences.zh: 夫中人已下，修辭力學者，則躁進患失，思展其用；

translations.literal: Among those of middling talent and below, those who polish their prose and strive in learning become restless in advance and fearful in loss, thinking to display their use;
translations.idiomatic: Among those of middling talent and below, those who polish their prose and strive in learning become restless in advance and fearful in loss, thinking to display their use;

sentences.zh: 審命知退者，則業荒文蕪，一不足采。

translations.literal: those who examine fate and know when to withdraw let their work grow barren and their writing overgrown, and one line is not worth gathering.
translations.idiomatic: those who examine fate and know when to withdraw let their work grow barren and their writing overgrown, and one line is not worth gathering.

sentences.zh: 唯上智則研其慮，博其聞，堅其習，精其業，用之則行，舍之則藏。

translations.literal: Only the highest wisdom refines its thought, broadens its hearing, strengthens its practice, and perfects its craft—employed, it acts; set aside, it hides.
translations.idiomatic: Only the highest wisdom refines its thought, broadens its hearing, strengthens its practice, and perfects its craft—employed, it acts; set aside, it hides.

sentences.zh: 茍異於斯，豈爲君子？

translations.literal: If one differs from this, how can one be called a gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: If one differs from this, how can one be called a gentleman?

sentences.zh: 初公綽理家甚嚴，子弟克稟誡訓，言家法者，世稱柳氏云。

translations.literal: From the first Gongchuo governed the household with great strictness; the sons and younger brothers were able to receive his admonitions, and when people spoke of family rules, the world called them the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: From the first Gongchuo governed the household with great strictness; the sons and younger brothers were able to receive his admonitions, and when people spoke of family rules, the world called them the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 公權，字誠懇。

translations.literal: Gongquan, styled Chenken.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan, styled Chenken.

sentences.zh: 幼嗜學，十二能爲辭賦。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning; at twelve he could compose rhapsodies and fu.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning; at twelve he could compose rhapsodies and fu.

sentences.zh: 元和初，進士擢第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office became a proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and took his first post as proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李聽鎭夏州，辟爲掌書記。

translations.literal: When Li Ting governed Xia Prefecture, he recruited Gongquan as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ting governed Xia Prefecture, he recruited Gongquan as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，入奏事，帝召見，謂公權曰：「我於佛寺見卿筆跡，思之久矣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Gongquan entered to report affairs; the emperor summoned him and addressed Gongquan: "I saw your handwriting at a Buddhist temple and have long thought of you."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Gongquan entered to report affairs; the emperor summoned him and told Gongquan, "I saw your handwriting at a Buddhist temple and have long thought of you."

sentences.zh: 即日拜右拾遺，充翰林侍書學士。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Right Reminder and made Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed Right Reminder and made Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher Academician.

sentences.zh: 遷右補闕、司封員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 穆宗政僻，嘗問公權筆何盡善，對曰：「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong's governance was eccentric; he once asked Gongquan why his brushwork was entirely excellent, and he replied: "The brush is used in the heart; when the heart is upright, the brush is upright."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong's governance was eccentric; he once asked Gongquan why his brushwork was entirely excellent, and he replied, "The brush is used in the heart; when the heart is upright, the brush is upright."

sentences.zh: 上改容，知其筆諫也。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression, knowing this was brushwork remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed expression, knowing this was remonstrance through calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 歴穆、敬、文三朝，侍書中禁。

translations.literal: Through the Muzong, Jing, and Wen reigns he served as calligrapher within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Muzong, Jing, and Wen reigns he served as calligrapher within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 公綽在太原，致書於宰相李宗閔云：「家弟苦心辭藝，先朝以侍書見用，頗偕工祝，心實恥之，乞換一散秩。」

translations.literal: Gongchuo, in Taiyuan, wrote to Chancellor Li Zongmin: "My younger brother has labored at literary craft; the former court employed him as attendant calligrapher, which put him rather on a level with artisans and prayer-writers—he is truly ashamed and begs to be exchanged for some ordinary post."
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo, in Taiyuan, wrote to Chancellor Li Zongmin, "My younger brother has labored at literary craft; the former court employed him as attendant calligrapher, which put him rather on a level with artisans and prayer-writers—he is truly ashamed and begs to be exchanged for some ordinary post."

sentences.zh: 乃遷右司郎中，累換司封、兵部二郎中、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to Right Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and after successive changes became Vice Director in the Ministries of Rites and War and Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was transferred to Right Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and after successive changes became Vice Director in the Ministries of Rites and War and Academician of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 文嘗思之，復召侍書，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen missed him and again summoned him as attendant calligrapher, promoting him to Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen missed him and again summoned him as attendant calligrapher, promoting him to Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 俄改中書舍人，充翰林書詔學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Attendant of the Secretariat and made Hanlin Academician for Imperial Script.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Attendant of the Secretariat and made Hanlin Academician for Imperial Script.

sentences.zh: 毎浴堂召對，繼燭見跋，語猶未盡，不欲取燭，宮人以蠟涙揉紙繼之。

translations.literal: Every time he was summoned for audience in the Bathing Hall, when the added candles burned down to the socket and his words were still unfinished, unwilling to take more candles, palace women kneaded wax tears into paper to continue the light.
translations.idiomatic: Every time he was summoned for audience in the Bathing Hall, when the added candles burned down to the socket and his words were still unfinished, unwilling to take more candles, palace women kneaded wax drippings into paper to continue the light.

sentences.zh: 從幸未央宮，苑中駐輦謂公權曰：「我有一喜事，邊上衣賜，久不及時，今年二月給春衣訖。」

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Weiyang Palace, the emperor halted his carriage in the park and told Gongquan: "I have a happy matter: grants of clothing to the frontier armies have long missed the season, but this year in the second month spring clothing was issued."
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Weiyang Palace, the emperor halted his carriage in the park and told Gongquan, "I have a happy matter: grants of clothing to the frontier armies have long missed the season, but this year in the second month spring clothing was issued."

sentences.zh: 公權前奉賀，上曰：「單賀未了，卿可賀我以詩。」

translations.literal: Gongquan stepped forward to offer congratulations; the emperor said: "A single congratulation is not enough—you may congratulate me with a poem."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan stepped forward to offer congratulations; the emperor said, "A single congratulation is not enough—you may congratulate me with a poem."

sentences.zh: 宮人迫其口進，公權應聲曰：「去歳雖無戰，今年未得歸。

translations.literal: Palace women pressed at his mouth for him to proceed; Gongquan answered on the spot: "Last year though there was no war, this year we have not yet returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women pressed at his mouth for him to proceed; Gongquan answered on the spot, "Last year though there was no war, this year we have not yet returned home.

sentences.zh: 皇恩何以報，春日得春衣。」

translations.literal: How may imperial grace be repaid? In spring we received spring clothing."
translations.idiomatic: How may imperial grace be repaid? In spring we received spring clothing."

sentences.zh: 上悅，激賞久之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and praised him warmly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and praised him warmly for a long time.

sentences.zh: 便殿對六學士，上語及漢文恭儉，帝舉袂曰：「此浣濯者三矣。」

translations.literal: In a side hall he faced the six academicians; the emperor spoke of Emperor Wen of Han's respectful frugality and raised his sleeve: "This has been washed three times."
translations.idiomatic: In a side hall he faced the six academicians; the emperor spoke of Emperor Wen of Han's respectful frugality and raised his sleeve, "This has been washed three times."

sentences.zh: 學士皆贊詠帝之儉德，唯公權無言。

translations.literal: The academicians all praised and extolled the emperor's frugal virtue; only Gongquan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The academicians all praised and extolled the emperor's frugal virtue; only Gongquan was silent.

sentences.zh: 帝留而問之，對曰：「人主當進賢良，退不肖，納諫諍，明賞罰。

translations.literal: The emperor kept him and questioned him; he replied: "A ruler should advance the worthy and good, remove the unworthy, accept remonstrance, and make rewards and punishments clear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept him and questioned him; he replied, "A ruler should advance the worthy and good, remove the unworthy, accept remonstrance, and make rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 服浣濯之衣，乃小節耳。」

translations.literal: Wearing washed clothes is only a small matter."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing washed clothes is only a small matter."

sentences.zh: 時周墀同對，爲之股栗，公權辭氣不可奪。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Chi was also in audience; his thighs trembled for Gongquan, but Gongquan's tone could not be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou Chi was also in audience; his thighs trembled for Gongquan, but Gongquan's tone could not be shaken.

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「極知舍人不合作諫議，以卿言事有諍臣風彩，卻授卿諫議大夫。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "I fully know the Academician should not have been made Remonstrance Counselor; because in your remonstrances you have the bearing of a loyal critic, I instead appoint you Remonstrance Counselor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I know perfectly well an Academician ought not to hold the post of Remonstrance Counselor—but because your remonstrances carry the spirit of a true critic, I am giving you that office instead."

sentences.zh: 翌日降制，以諫議知制誥，學士如故。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued appointing him Remonstrance Counselor and Director of Imperial Edicts, with his post as Academician unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The following day an edict named him Remonstrance Counselor with concurrent duty as Director of Imperial Edicts, while he retained his Academician post.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，轉工部侍郎，充職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works, continuing in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 838, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 嘗入對，上謂曰：「近日外議如何？」

translations.literal: Once when he came for audience, the emperor asked him, "What is the recent talk outside?"
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion when he came for audience, the emperor asked, "What are people saying outside lately?"

sentences.zh: 公權對曰：「自郭旼除授邠寧，物議頗有臧否。」

translations.literal: Gongquan replied, "Since Guo Min was appointed to Binning, public opinion has been quite mixed."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan answered, "Since Guo Min's appointment to Binning, there has been considerable praise and blame in public talk."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「旼是尚父之從子，太皇太后之季父，在官無過。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Min is the late Prince of Shang's cousin and the Great Empress Dowager's youngest uncle; in office he has committed no fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Min is a cousin of the late Prince of Shang and the Great Empress Dowager's youngest uncle. In office he has done nothing wrong.

sentences.zh: 自金吾大將授邠寧小鎭，何事議論耶？」

translations.literal: From Commandant of the Gold Crow Guards to a small border command at Binning—what is there to discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: He went from Commandant of the Gold Crow Guards to a minor frontier post at Binning—what is there to debate?"

sentences.zh: 公權曰：「以旼勛德，除鎭攸宜。

translations.literal: Gongquan said, "Given Min's merits and virtue, his appointment to a command is entirely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan said, "Given Min's achievements and virtue, appointing him to a command is entirely appropriate.

sentences.zh: 人情論議者，言旼進二女入宮，致此除拜，此信乎？」

translations.literal: What people are discussing is that Min sent two daughters into the palace, leading to this appointment—is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: What people are saying is that Min advanced two daughters into the palace and thereby won this appointment—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「二女入宮參太后，非獻也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The two daughters entered the palace to attend the Empress Dowager—they were not offered as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The two daughters entered the palace to wait upon the Empress Dowager. They were not presented as tribute."

sentences.zh: 公權曰：「瓜李之嫌，何以戸曉？」

translations.literal: Gongquan said, "Even the suspicion of 'melon by the path, plum beneath the tree'—how can every household understand?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan said, "Even the shadow of impropriety—how can every household see through it?"

sentences.zh: 因引王珪諫太宗出廬江王妃故事。

translations.literal: He then cited the story of Wang Gui remonstrating with Taizong to send away the Princess of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited the precedent of Wang Gui remonstrating with Emperor Taizong to send away the Princess of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 帝即令南内使張日華送二女還旼。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered the Southern Inner Palace envoy Zhang Rihua to return the two daughters to Min.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered Zhang Rihua, envoy of the Southern Inner Palace, to send the two daughters back to Min.

sentences.zh: 公權忠言匡益，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Gongquan's loyal words that corrected and benefited the state were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan's loyal remonstrances that corrected and strengthened the government were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 累遷學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，罷内職，授右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Gongquan was removed from inner-court posts and appointed Right Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, Gongquan was dismissed from inner-court office and appointed Right Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔珙用爲集賢學士、判院事。

translations.literal: Chancellor Cui Gong employed him as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Cui Gong appointed him Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with supervisory charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 李德裕素待公權厚，及爲珙奏薦，頗不悅。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had always treated Gongquan generously, and when Gong was recommended by Cui, he was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had always treated Gongquan well, and when Cui recommended him, Li was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 左授太子詹事，改賓客。

translations.literal: Gongquan was demoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then changed to Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then reassigned as Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 累遷金紫光祿大夫、上柱國、河東郡開國公、食邑二千戸。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with Golden Ornament, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Hedong Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with Golden Ornament, Upper Pillar of the State, and Duke of Hedong Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 復爲左常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He again served as Left Regular Palace Attendant and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Left Regular Palace Attendant and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 歴工部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，改太子少傅，改少師，居三品、二品班三十年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong, he was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, then Junior Mentor, and for thirty years held third- and second-rank court positions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantong era he became Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, then Junior Mentor, and for thirty years stood in the third- and second-rank court ranks.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，贈太子太師，時年八十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died and was posthumously given the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; he was eighty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. He was eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 公權初學王書，遍閲近代筆法，體勢勁媚，自成一家。

translations.literal: Gongquan first studied Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, thoroughly reviewed recent brush techniques, and developed a vigorous yet graceful style all his own.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan began by studying Wang Xizhi's calligraphy, surveyed the brush methods of recent masters, and forged a vigorous, graceful style entirely his own.

sentences.zh: 當時公卿大臣家碑板，不得公權手筆者，人以爲不孝。

translations.literal: At the time, for steles and plaques in the homes of high officials and great ministers, if they did not bear Gongquan's own handwriting, people regarded it as unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, for steles and plaques in the households of ministers and great officials, those that lacked Gongquan's own brushwork were thought unfilial.

sentences.zh: 外夷入貢，皆別署貨貝，曰此購柳書。

translations.literal: When foreign peoples brought tribute, they all set aside goods separately, saying these were to purchase Liu's calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys brought tribute, they all set aside goods separately, marked as payment for Liu's calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 上都西明寺《金剛經碑》備有鍾、王、歐、虞、褚、陸之體，尤爲得意。

translations.literal: His Diamond Sutra stele at Ximing Temple in the capital embodied the styles of Zhong, Wang, Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu, and was especially a work he was proud of.
translations.idiomatic: His Diamond Sutra stele at Ximing Temple in the capital united the manners of Zhong, Wang, Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu, and was among the works he prized most.

sentences.zh: 文宗夏日與學士聯句，帝曰：「人皆苦炎熱，我愛夏日長。」

translations.literal: On a summer day Wenzong joined academicians in linked verse; the emperor said, "All men suffer the blazing heat—I love how long the summer day is."
translations.idiomatic: On a summer day Wenzong joined the academicians in linked verse. The emperor opened with, "All men chafe at the heat—I love how long the summer day is."

sentences.zh: 公權續曰：「薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼。」

translations.literal: Gongquan continued, "The balmy breeze comes from the south, and the palace halls breathe a subtle cool."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan answered, "The balmy breeze comes from the south, and the palace halls breathe a subtle cool."

sentences.zh: 時丁、袁五學士皆屬繼，帝獨諷公權兩句，曰：「辭淸意足，不可多得。」

translations.literal: At the time the five academicians Ding and Yuan all contributed in turn, but the emperor singled out Gongquan's two lines alone, saying, "The wording is clear and the meaning complete—such lines are hard to come by."
translations.idiomatic: The five academicians of the Ding and Yuan families all added lines in turn, but the emperor singled out Gongquan's couplet alone, saying, "The language is clear and the thought complete—lines like these are rare."

sentences.zh: 乃令公權題於殿壁，字方圓五寸，帝視之，嘆曰：「鍾、王復生，無以加焉！」

translations.literal: He then ordered Gongquan to inscribe them on the hall wall in characters five inches square; when the emperor looked upon them he exclaimed, "If Zhong and Wang were reborn, they could add nothing more!"
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Gongquan to write the lines on the hall wall in five-inch-square characters. When the emperor saw them he sighed, "If Zhong and Wang were reborn, they could add nothing more!"

sentences.zh: 大中初，轉少師，中謝，宣宗召升殿，御前書三紙，軍容使西門季玄捧硯，樞密使崔巨源過筆。

translations.literal: Early in Dazhong, upon becoming Junior Mentor and offering thanks at court, Xuanzong summoned him to ascend the hall; before the throne the emperor wrote on three sheets—the Commissioner of Army Affairs Ximen Jixuan held the inkstone, and the Commissioner of Military Affairs Cui Juyuan passed the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong era, when Gongquan became Junior Mentor and came to offer thanks at court, Xuanzong summoned him up the hall. Before the throne the emperor wrote on three sheets—Army Affairs Commissioner Ximen Jixuan held the inkstone while Military Affairs Commissioner Cui Juyuan passed the brush.

sentences.zh: 一紙眞書十字，曰「衞夫人傳筆法於王右軍」；

translations.literal: On one sheet in standard script, ten characters: "Lady Wei transmitted brush methods to Wang, General of the Right."
translations.idiomatic: On one sheet in standard script, ten characters: "Lady Wei transmitted brush methods to Wang, General of the Right."

sentences.zh: 一紙行書十一字，曰「永禪師眞草《千字文》得家法」；

translations.literal: On one sheet in running script, eleven characters: "Monk Yong's standard and cursive Thousand-Character Classic attained the family tradition."
translations.idiomatic: On one sheet in running script, eleven characters: "Monk Yong's standard and cursive Thousand-Character Classic mastered the family tradition."

sentences.zh: 一紙草書八字，曰「謂語助者焉哉乎也」。

translations.literal: On one sheet in cursive script, eight characters: "As for the particles—yan, zai, hu, ye."
translations.idiomatic: On one sheet in cursive script, eight characters: "As for the particles—yan, zai, hu, ye."

sentences.zh: 賜錦彩、甁盤等銀器，仍令自書謝狀，勿拘眞行，帝尤奇惜之。

translations.literal: He was granted brocades, vases, dishes, and other silver vessels, and was also told to write his own letter of thanks without restricting himself to standard or running script; the emperor especially treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: He received brocades, vases, dishes, and other silver vessels, and was told to write his own letter of thanks in whatever script he chose. The emperor treasured it all the more.

sentences.zh: 公權志耽書學，不能治生；

translations.literal: Gongquan was devoted heart and soul to calligraphy and scholarship and could not manage household affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan devoted himself wholly to calligraphy and learning and could not manage his household affairs;

sentences.zh: 爲勛戚家碑板，問遺歳時鉅萬，多爲主藏豎海鷗、龍安所竊。

translations.literal: for steles he wrote for meritorious kin, gifts amounted to tens of thousands each year, but much was stolen by the household stewards Hai'ou and Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: for steles he wrote for meritorious kinsmen, gifts ran to tens of thousands each year, yet much was stolen by his chief stewards Hai'ou and Long'an.

sentences.zh: 別貯酒器杯盂一笥，緘滕如故，其器皆亡。

translations.literal: He stored wine vessels, cups, and bowls in a separate chest with the seal intact, yet the vessels were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: He kept wine vessels, cups, and bowls in a separate chest, the seal still intact—and the vessels were all gone.

sentences.zh: 訊海鷗，乃曰：「不測其亡。」

translations.literal: When he questioned Hai'ou, the man said, "I cannot fathom how they vanished."
translations.idiomatic: When he questioned Hai'ou, the man answered, "I cannot fathom how they disappeared."

sentences.zh: 公權哂曰：「銀杯羽化耳。」

translations.literal: Gongquan gave a wry smile and said, "The silver cups have transformed and ascended."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan smiled wryly and said, "The silver cups have transformed and ascended."

sentences.zh: 不復更言。

translations.literal: He said no more about it.
translations.idiomatic: He said no more about it.

sentences.zh: 所寶唯筆硯圖畫，自扃鐍之。

translations.literal: What he treasured were only brushes, inkstones, and paintings, which he locked away himself.
translations.idiomatic: What he treasured were only brushes, inkstones, and paintings, which he locked away himself.

sentences.zh: 常評硯，以靑州石末爲第一，言墨易冷，絳州黑硯次之。

translations.literal: He often ranked inkstones, placing Qingzhou stone dust first; as he remarked, ink easily grows cold—Jiangzhou black inkstones came next.
translations.idiomatic: He often ranked inkstones, placing Qingzhou stone dust first; as he remarked, ink easily grows cold—Jiangzhou black inkstones came next.

sentences.zh: 尤精《左氏傳》、《國語》、《尚書》、《毛詩》、《莊子》。

translations.literal: He was especially accomplished in the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Documents, Mao's Odes, and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in the Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, Documents, Mao's Odes, and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 毎説一義，必誦數紙。

translations.literal: Whenever he expounded a point, he would recite several sheets of text.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he expounded a point, he would recite several sheets of text from memory.

sentences.zh: 性曉音律，不好奏樂。

translations.literal: By nature he understood musical pitch, yet he disliked having music played.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he understood musical pitch, yet he disliked having music performed.

sentences.zh: 常云：「聞樂令人驕怠故也。」

translations.literal: He often said, "Hearing music makes men proud and slack—that is why."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Hearing music makes men proud and slack—that is why I avoid it."

sentences.zh: 公綽伯父子華，永泰初，爲嚴武西蜀判官，奏爲成都令。

translations.literal: Gongchuo, elder brother of Gongquan's father Zihua—in the beginning of Yongtai served as western Shu aide to Yan Wu and was recommended as magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo, elder brother of Gongquan's father Zihua—in the beginning of the Yongtai era served as Yan Wu's western Shu aide and was recommended as magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 累遷池州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to prefect of Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to prefect of Chi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入爲昭應令，知府東十三縣捕賊，尋檢校金部郎中、修葺華淸宮使。

translations.literal: He entered service as magistrate of Zhaoying, took charge of capturing bandits in the thirteen eastern counties of the metropolitan district, and soon served as acting director in the Ministry of Revenue and Commissioner for Repair of Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as magistrate of Zhaoying, took charge of capturing bandits in the thirteen eastern counties of the metropolitan district, and soon served as acting director in the Ministry of Revenue and Commissioner for Repair of Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 元載欲用爲京兆尹，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai wished to appoint him metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, but before he received the appointment he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai wished to appoint him metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, but he died before the appointment was issued.

sentences.zh: 自知死日，預爲墓誌。

translations.literal: Knowing the day of his death in advance, he prepared his epitaph beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the day of his death in advance, he prepared his epitaph beforehand.

sentences.zh: 有知人之明。

translations.literal: He had the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for judging men.

sentences.zh: 公綽生三日，視之，謂其弟子温曰：「保惜此兒，福祚吾兄弟不能及。

translations.literal: When Gongchuo was three days old, Zihua looked at him and told his younger brother Wen, "Cherish this boy—the fortune and rank of us brothers cannot match his.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongchuo was three days old, Zihua looked at him and told his younger brother Wen, "Cherish this boy. The fortune and rank of us brothers cannot equal his.

sentences.zh: 興吾門者，此兒也。」

translations.literal: He who will raise our house is this boy."
translations.idiomatic: The one who will raise our house is this boy."

sentences.zh: 因以起之爲公綽字。

translations.literal: He therefore took Qi as Gongchuo's style name.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took Qi as Gongchuo's style name.

sentences.zh: 子華二子：公器、公度。

translations.literal: Zihua had two sons: Gongqi and Gongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua had two sons: Gongqi and Gongdu.

sentences.zh: 公度善攝生，年八十餘，歩履輕便。

translations.literal: Gongdu was skilled at nurturing life; past eighty, his gait was still light.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdu was skilled at nurturing life; past eighty, he still walked lightly.

sentences.zh: 或祈其術，曰：「吾初無術，但未嘗以元氣佐喜怒，氣海常温耳！」

translations.literal: When some asked his method, he said, "I had no method at first—I simply never let anger or joy disturb my vital breath; the sea of breath stays warm, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: When some asked his secret, he said, "I had no method at first—I simply never let anger or joy disturb my vital breath. The sea of breath stays warm, that is all!"

sentences.zh: 位止光祿少卿。

translations.literal: His rank stopped at Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose no higher than Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 公器子遵。

translations.literal: Gongqi's son was Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Gongqi's son was Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵子璨。

translations.literal: Zun's son was Can.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son was Can.

sentences.zh: 璨仕至宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: Can rose to chancellor and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose to chancellor and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 崔玄亮，字晦叔，山東磁州人也。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanliang, styled Huishu, was a man of Cizhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang, styled Huishu, was a native of Cizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 玄亮貞元十一年登進士第，從事諸侯府。

translations.literal: Xuanliang passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Zhenyuan and served in various regional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang passed the jinshi examination in 795 and served in the staffs of various lords.

sentences.zh: 性雅淡，好道術，不樂趨競，久遊江湖。

translations.literal: His nature was refined and detached; he loved Daoist arts and disliked scrambling for advancement, and for a long time wandered the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and detached by nature, he loved Daoist arts, disliked scrambling for advancement, and for years wandered the rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 至元和初，因知己薦達入朝。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Yuanhe era, through a patron's recommendation he entered court service.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Yuanhe era, a patron's recommendation brought him into court service.

sentences.zh: 再遷監察御史，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to investigating censor, then transferred to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted twice to investigating censor, then transferred to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 出爲密、湖、曹三郡刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Mi, Hu, and Cao—the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as prefect of Mi, Hu, and Cao Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 毎一遷秩，謙讓輒形於色。

translations.literal: With each promotion his humility showed plainly on his face.
translations.idiomatic: With each promotion his humility showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 太和初，入爲太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, he entered service as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era he entered service as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜諫議大夫，中謝日，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Remonstrance Counselor; on the day he offered thanks at court, he was personally granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In 830 he was appointed Remonstrance Counselor; on the day he offered thanks at court, he was personally granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 朝廷推其名望，遷右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The court valued his reputation and promoted him to Right Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued his standing and promoted him to Right Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 來年，宰相宋申錫爲鄭註所構，獄自内起，京師震懼。

translations.literal: The following year Chancellor Song Shenxi was framed by Zheng Zhu; the case arose from within the palace, and the capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chancellor Song Shenxi was framed by Zheng Zhu. The case arose from within the palace, and the capital trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 玄亮首率諫官十四人，詣延英請對，與文宗往復數百言。

translations.literal: Xuanliang was the first to lead fourteen remonstrance officials to the Yanying Hall to request audience, exchanging several hundred words back and forth with Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang was the first to lead fourteen remonstrance officials to the Yanying Hall to request audience, exchanging several hundred words with Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 文宗初不省其諫，欲置申錫於法。

translations.literal: At first Wenzong did not grasp their remonstrance and intended to punish Shenxi by law.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wenzong did not take in their remonstrance and intended to punish Shenxi by law.

sentences.zh: 玄亮泣奏曰：「孟軻有言：衆人皆曰殺之，未可也；

translations.literal: Xuanliang wept as he submitted, "Mencius has a saying: when all the common people say kill him, it is not yet permissible;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang wept as he submitted, "Mencius said: when all the common people say kill him, it is not yet permissible;

sentences.zh: 卿大夫皆曰殺之，未可也；

translations.literal: when all the ministers and grandees say kill him, it is not yet permissible;
translations.idiomatic: when all the ministers and grandees say kill him, it is not yet permissible;

sentences.zh: 天下皆曰殺之，然後察之，方置於法。

translations.literal: when all under Heaven say kill him, then examine the matter, and only then apply the law.
translations.idiomatic: when all under Heaven say kill him, then examine the matter, and only then apply the law.

sentences.zh: 今至聖之代，殺一凡庶，尚須合於典法，況無辜殺一宰相乎？

translations.literal: In this age of utmost sagacity, even killing a common man must accord with the statutes—how much more must one not kill a guiltless chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: In this age of utmost sagacity, even killing a common man must accord with the statutes—how much less may one kill a guiltless chancellor?

sentences.zh: 臣爲陛下惜天下法，實不爲申錫也。」

translations.literal: I grieve for the laws of the realm on Your Majesty's behalf—it is truly not for Shenxi's sake."
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for the laws of the realm on Your Majesty's behalf—it is truly not for Shenxi's sake."

sentences.zh: 言訖，俯伏嗚咽，文宗爲之感悟。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he bowed prostrate and sobbed; Wenzong was moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished he bowed prostrate and sobbed, and Wenzong was moved to understanding.

sentences.zh: 玄亮由此名重於朝。

translations.literal: From this Xuanliang's name weighed heavily at court.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xuanliang's name weighed heavily at court.

sentences.zh: 七年，以疾求爲外任；

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on account of illness he requested an outer appointment;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on account of illness he requested an outer appointment;

sentences.zh: 宰相以弘農便其所請。

translations.literal: the chancellor thought Hongnong suited his request.
translations.idiomatic: the chancellor thought Hongnong suited his request.

sentences.zh: 乃授檢校左散騎常侍、虢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歳七月，卒於郡所，中外無不嘆惜。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month he died in his prefecture; within and without the court all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the seventh month he died in his prefecture; within and without the court all mourned him.

sentences.zh: 始玄亮登第，弟純亮、寅亮相次升進士科。

translations.literal: When Xuanliang first passed the examination, his younger brothers Chunliang and Yinliang passed the jinshi in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanliang first passed the examination, his younger brothers Chunliang and Yinliang passed the jinshi in succession.

sentences.zh: 蕃府辟召，而玄亮最達。

translations.literal: Frontier headquarters all recruited them, but Xuanliang rose highest.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier headquarters all recruited them, but Xuanliang rose highest.

sentences.zh: 玄亮孫貽孫，位至侍郎。

translations.literal: Xuanliang's grandson Yisun rose to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang's grandson Yisun rose to Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 温造，字簡輿，河内人。

translations.literal: Wen Zao, styled Jian-yu, was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zao, styled Jian-yu, was a native of Henei.

sentences.zh: 祖景倩，南鄭令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jingqian was magistrate of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jingqian was magistrate of Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 父輔國，太常丞。

translations.literal: His father Fuguo was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fuguo was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 造幼嗜學，不喜試吏，自負節概，少所降志，隱居王屋，以漁釣逍遙爲事。

translations.literal: From childhood Zao loved learning and disliked taking office; confident in his integrity, he seldom bowed his will, lived in seclusion on Mount Wangwu, and made fishing and angling his free life.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zao loved learning and disliked taking office. Confident in his integrity, he seldom bowed his will, lived in seclusion on Mount Wangwu, and made fishing and angling his free life.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張建封聞風致書幣招延，造欣然謂所親曰：「此可人也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shou Prefecture, hearing of his reputation sent letters and gifts to invite him; Zao gladly told those close to him, "This is a man one may serve."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, prefect of Shou Prefecture, hearing of his reputation sent letters and gifts to invite him. Zao gladly told those close to him, "This is a man one may serve."

sentences.zh: 徙家從之。

translations.literal: He moved his household to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his household to follow him.

sentences.zh: 建封動靜咨詢，而不敢縻以職任。

translations.literal: Jianfeng consulted him on every move, yet dared not bind him with an official post.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng consulted him on every move, yet dared not bind him with an official post.

sentences.zh: 及建封授節彭門，造歸下邳，有髙天下之心。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng received his command at Pengmen, Zao returned to Xiapi with a heart set on transcending the world.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng received his command at Pengmen, Zao returned to Xiapi with a heart set on transcending the world.

sentences.zh: 建封恐一旦失造，乃以兄女妻之。

translations.literal: Jianfeng feared he might lose Zao at any moment and therefore gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng feared he might lose Zao at any moment and therefore gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈方悖，侵寇籓鄰，屢陷郡邑。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xilie was in rebellion, invading neighboring commands and repeatedly capturing prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Xilie was in rebellion, invading neighboring commands and repeatedly capturing prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 天下城鎭恃兵者，從而動搖，多逐主帥，自立留後，邀求節鉞。

translations.literal: Fortresses throughout the realm that relied on troops followed suit in wavering; many expelled their commanders, installed themselves as acting commissioners, and demanded command seals.
translations.idiomatic: Fortresses throughout the realm that relied on troops followed suit in wavering; many expelled their commanders, installed themselves as acting commissioners, and demanded command seals.

sentences.zh: 德宗患之，以范陽劉濟方輸忠款，但未能盡達朝廷倚賴之意；

translations.literal: Dezong was troubled by this; Liu Ji of Fanyang was then offering loyal submission, yet the court's reliance on him could not be fully conveyed;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was troubled by this. Liu Ji of Fanyang was then offering loyal submission, yet the court's reliance on him could not be fully conveyed;

sentences.zh: 與密詔建封選特達識略之士往喩之。

translations.literal: he secretly ordered Jianfeng to select a man of exceptional insight and strategy to go explain this to him.
translations.idiomatic: he secretly ordered Jianfeng to select a man of exceptional insight and strategy to go explain this to him.

sentences.zh: 建封乃強署造節度參謀，使於幽州。

translations.literal: Jianfeng therefore forcibly appointed Zao military staff officer of the command and sent him to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng therefore forcibly appointed Zao military staff officer of the command and sent him to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 造與語未訖，濟俯伏流涕曰：「濟僻在遐裔，不知天子神聖，大臣忠藎。

translations.literal: Before Zao had finished speaking with him, Ji bowed prostrate and wept, "Ji dwells in a remote borderland and did not know the Son of Heaven's sagacity, nor the loyalty of great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zao had finished speaking with him, Ji bowed prostrate and wept, "Ji dwells in a remote borderland and did not know the Son of Heaven's sagacity, nor the loyalty of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 願得率先諸侯，效以死節。」

translations.literal: I wish to take the lead among all lords and pledge my life in loyal service."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to take the lead among all lords and pledge my life in loyal service."

sentences.zh: 造還，建封以其名上聞。

translations.literal: When Zao returned, Jianfeng reported his name to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao returned, Jianfeng reported his name to the throne.

sentences.zh: 德宗愛其才，召至京師，謂之曰：「卿誰家子？

translations.literal: Dezong admired his talent and summoned him to the capital, asking him, "Whose son are you?
translations.idiomatic: Dezong admired his talent and summoned him to the capital, asking, "Whose son are you?

sentences.zh: 年復幾何？」

translations.literal: How many years have you?"
translations.idiomatic: How many years have you?"

sentences.zh: 造對曰：「臣五代祖大雅，外五代祖李勣。

translations.literal: Zao replied, "My fifth-generation ancestor was Daya; on my mother's side the fifth-generation ancestor was Li Jixu.
translations.idiomatic: Zao replied, "My fifth-generation ancestor was Daya; on my mother's side the fifth-generation ancestor was Li Jixu.

sentences.zh: 臣犬馬之年三十有二。」

translations.literal: In the years of a hound and horse I am thirty-two."
translations.idiomatic: In the years of a hound and horse I am thirty-two."

sentences.zh: 德宗奇之，欲用爲諫官，以語泄事寢。

translations.literal: Dezong marveled at him and wished to appoint him a remonstrance official, but because the plan leaked the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong marveled at him and wished to appoint him a remonstrance official, but because the plan leaked the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，授京兆府司録參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he was appointed Recorder of Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 821 he was appointed Recorder of Jingzhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奉使河朔稱旨，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Hebei region he pleased the throne and was promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Hebei region he pleased the throne and was promoted to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 既而幽州劉總請以所部九州聽朝旨。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liu Zong of Youzhou requested that his nine prefectures submit to court authority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Zong of Youzhou requested that his nine prefectures submit to court authority.

sentences.zh: 穆宗選可使者，或薦造。

translations.literal: Muzong chose someone fit to go as envoy; some recommended Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong chose someone fit to go as envoy; some recommended Zao.

sentences.zh: 帝召而謂之曰：「朕以劉總輸忠，雖書詔便蕃，未盡朕之深意。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and said, "I regard Liu Zong's loyal submission; though written edicts reach the frontier, they do not fully convey my deeper intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and said, "I regard Liu Zong's loyal submission. Though written edicts reach the frontier, they do not fully convey my deeper intent.

sentences.zh: 以卿素能辦事，爲朕此行。」

translations.literal: Because you have always been able to handle affairs, go on this mission for me."
translations.idiomatic: Because you have always been able to handle affairs, go on this mission for me."

sentences.zh: 造對曰：「臣府縣走吏，初受憲職，望輕事重，恐辱國命，無能諭旨。」

translations.literal: Zao replied, "I am a runner from prefecture and county offices, newly receiving an inspector's post; my standing is light and the task heavy—I fear I will disgrace the imperial command and fail to convey Your Majesty's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zao replied, "I am a runner from prefecture and county offices, newly receiving an inspector's post. My standing is light and the task heavy—I fear I will disgrace the imperial command and fail to convey Your Majesty's intent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我在東宮時，聞劉總請覲；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When I was in the Eastern Palace I heard that Liu Zong requested audience;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I was in the Eastern Palace I heard that Liu Zong requested audience;

sentences.zh: 及我即位，比年上書不絶，及約以行期，即喑默不報。

translations.literal: after I ascended the throne he sent memorial after memorial for years, and when an appointment for his journey was set, he fell silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: after I ascended the throne he sent memorial after memorial for years, and when an appointment for his journey was set, he fell silent and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 卿識機知變，往喩我懷，無多讓也。」

translations.literal: You read the moment and know how to change—go explain my heart, and do not decline overmuch."
translations.idiomatic: You read the moment and know how to change—go explain my heart, and do not decline overmuch."

sentences.zh: 乃拜起居舍人，賜緋魚袋，充太原、鎭州、幽州宣諭使。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Attendant on the Heir Apparent, granted the crimson robe and fish tally, and made Imperial Envoy to Taiyuan, Zhen Prefecture, and Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed Attendant on the Heir Apparent, granted the crimson robe and fish tally, and made Imperial Envoy to Taiyuan, Zhen Prefecture, and Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 造初至范陽，劉總具櫜鞬郊迎；

translations.literal: When Zao first reached Fanyang, Liu Zong fully equipped himself with bow case and quiver and met him beyond the suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: When Zao first reached Fanyang, Liu Zong fully equipped himself with bow case and quiver and met him beyond the suburbs;

sentences.zh: 乃宣聖旨，示以禍福。

translations.literal: Zao then proclaimed the sacred edict and showed him fortune and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zao then proclaimed the sacred edict and showed him fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 總俯伏流汗，若兵加於頸矣。
