translations.literal: Zong bowed prostrate, sweating as though weapons were at his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Zong bowed prostrate, sweating as though weapons were at his neck.

sentences.zh: 及造使還，總遂移家入覲，朝廷遂以張弘靖代之。

translations.literal: When Zao's mission returned, Zong moved his household to attend court, and the court appointed Zhang Hongjing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao's mission returned, Zong moved his household to attend court, and the court appointed Zhang Hongjing to replace him.

sentences.zh: 及硃克融逐弘靖，鎭州殺田弘正，朝廷用兵，乃先令造銜命河東、魏博、澤潞、橫海、深冀、易定等道，喩以軍期，事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: When Zhu Kerong expelled Hongjing, Zhen Prefecture killed Tian Hongzheng, and the court took up arms, Zao was first sent with imperial orders to Hedong, Weibo, Zelu, Henghai, Shenji, Yiding, and other circuits to announce campaign deadlines; all pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kerong expelled Hongjing, Zhen Prefecture killed Tian Hongzheng, and the court took up arms, Zao was first sent with imperial orders to Hedong, Weibo, Zelu, Henghai, Shenji, Yiding, and other circuits to announce campaign deadlines. All pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄而坐與諫議大夫李景儉史館飲酒，景儉醉謁丞相，出造爲朗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was demoted for sitting and drinking with Remonstrance Counselor Li Jingjian at the Historiographical Institute; Jingjian, drunk, paid court to the chancellor, and Zao was sent out as prefect of Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was demoted for sitting and drinking with Remonstrance Counselor Li Jingjian at the Historiographical Institute. Jingjian, drunk, paid court to the chancellor, and Zao was sent out as prefect of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在任開後鄕渠九十七里，溉田二千頃，郡人獲利，乃名爲右史渠。

translations.literal: In office he opened the Houxiang Canal ninety-seven li, irrigating two thousand qing of fields; the people of the prefecture profited, and it was named the Right Historian Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In office he opened the Houxiang Canal ninety-seven li, irrigating two thousand qing of fields. The people of the prefecture profited, and it was named the Right Historian Canal.

sentences.zh: 居四年，召拜侍御史，請復置彈事硃衣、豸冠於外廊，大臣阻而不行。

translations.literal: After four years he was summoned and appointed Attendant Censor; he requested that the censorial red robe and unicorn cap for presenting charges be restored to the outer corridor, but great ministers blocked it and the request was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was summoned and appointed Attendant Censor. He requested that the censorial red robe and unicorn cap for presenting charges be restored to the outer corridor, but great ministers blocked it and the request was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 李祐自夏州入拜金吾，違制進馬一百五十匹。

translations.literal: Li You entered from Xia Prefecture to take the post of Commandant of the Gold Crow Guards and, violating regulations, presented one hundred fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Li You entered from Xia Prefecture to take the post of Commandant of the Gold Crow Guards and, violating regulations, presented one hundred fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 造正衙彈奏，祐股戰汗流。

translations.literal: Zao impeached him in the main court; You's thighs trembled and sweat poured.
translations.idiomatic: Zao impeached him in the main court. You's thighs trembled and sweat poured.

sentences.zh: 祐私謂人曰：「吾夜逾蔡州城擒呉元濟，未嘗心動，今日膽落於温御史。

translations.literal: You privately told others, "By night I scaled the walls of Cai Prefecture and captured Wu Yuanji without my heart ever faltering—today my courage fell before Censor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: You privately told others, "By night I scaled the walls of Cai Prefecture and captured Wu Yuanji without my heart ever faltering—today my courage fell before Censor Wen.

sentences.zh: 籲，可畏哉！」

translations.literal: Alas, how fearsome!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how fearsome!"

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中，再知雜事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Director in the Secretariat and again took charge of miscellaneous censorial business.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Director in the Secretariat and again took charge of miscellaneous censorial business.

sentences.zh: 尋拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 太和二年十一月，宮中昭德寺火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Taihe, fire broke out at Zhaode Temple within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of 828, fire broke out at Zhaode Temple within the palace.

sentences.zh: 寺在宣政殿東隔垣，火勢將及，宰臣、兩省、京兆尹、中尉、樞密，皆環立於日華門外，令神策兵士救之，晡後稍息。

translations.literal: The temple stood east of Xuanzheng Hall beyond the partition wall; as the blaze neared, chancellors, officials of the Two Departments, the metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, the commissioner of the Inner Palace, and the commissioner of military affairs all stood ringed outside Rihua Gate while Shence troops fought the fire; after the hour of shen it gradually died down.
translations.idiomatic: The temple stood east of Xuanzheng Hall beyond the partition wall. As the blaze neared, chancellors, officials of the Two Departments, the metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, the commissioner of the Inner Palace, and the commissioner of military affairs all stood ringed outside Rihua Gate while Shence troops fought the fire. After the hour of shen it gradually died down.

sentences.zh: 是日，唯臺官不到。

translations.literal: That day only the censorial officials did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: That day only the censorial officials did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 造奏曰：「昨宮中遺火，縁臺有系囚，恐縁爲奸，追集人吏堤防，所以至朝堂在後，臣請自罰三十直。

translations.literal: Zao submitted, "Yesterday fire broke out in the palace. Because the Censorate had prisoners in custody, fearing they might take advantage of the disorder I gathered clerks and officers to guard against it—therefore I reached the court hall later. I request to fine myself thirty zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zao submitted, "Yesterday fire broke out in the palace. Because the Censorate had prisoners in custody, fearing they might take advantage of the disorder I gathered clerks and officers to guard against it—therefore I reached the court hall later. I request to fine myself thirty zhi.

sentences.zh: 其兩巡使崔蠡、姚合火滅方到，請別議責罰。」

translations.literal: The two patrol commissioners Cui Li and Yao He arrived only after the fire was out—please consider separate penalties."
translations.idiomatic: The two patrol commissioners Cui Li and Yao He arrived only after the fire was out—please consider separate penalties."

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「事出非常，臺有囚系，官曹警備，亦爲周慮，即合待罪朝堂，候取進止。

translations.literal: The edict read, "The matter was extraordinary; the Censorate had prisoners in custody and the offices took precautions—this too was thorough forethought. You should have awaited judgment in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "The matter was extraordinary. The Censorate had prisoners in custody and the offices took precautions—this too was thorough forethought. You should have awaited judgment in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 量罰自許，事渉乖儀。

translations.literal: To set your own penalty was contrary to protocol.
translations.idiomatic: To set your own penalty was contrary to protocol.

sentences.zh: 温造、姚合、崔蠡各罰一月俸料。」

translations.literal: Wen Zao, Yao He, and Cui Li are each fined one month's salary."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zao, Yao He, and Cui Li are each fined one month's salary."

sentences.zh: 造性剛褊，人或激觸，不顧貴勢，以氣淩藉。

translations.literal: Zao's nature was stern and narrow; if someone provoked him he paid no heed to rank and power, and trampled others with his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's nature was stern and narrow. If someone provoked him he paid no heed to rank and power and trampled others with his spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇左補闕李虞於街，怒其不避，捕祗承人決脊十下。

translations.literal: Once he met Left Supplementation Officer Li Yu in the street, grew angry that Yu did not yield, and had his attendants seize and flog the bearer ten strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Left Supplementation Officer Li Yu in the street, grew angry that Yu did not yield, and had his attendants seize and flog the bearer ten strokes.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺舒元褒等上疎論之曰：「國朝故事，供奉官街中，除宰相外，無所回避。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Shu Yuanbao and others submitted a memorial arguing, "By the precedents of our dynasty, for palace attendants in the streets, apart from the chancellor, none need yield.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Shu Yuanbao and others submitted a memorial arguing, "By the precedents of our dynasty, for palace attendants in the streets, apart from the chancellor, none need yield.

sentences.zh: 温造蔑朝廷典禮，淩陛下侍臣，恣行胸臆，曾無畏忌。

translations.literal: Wen Zao scorned the court's ritual and trampled the emperor's attendants, giving free rein to his breast and never fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zao scorned the court's ritual and trampled the emperor's attendants, giving free rein to his breast and never fearing.

sentences.zh: 凡事有小而關分理者，不可失也。

translations.literal: In all affairs, what is small yet touches right principle must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: In all affairs, what is small yet touches right principle must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 分理一失，亂由之生。

translations.literal: Once right principle is lost, disorder arises from it.
translations.idiomatic: Once right principle is lost, disorder arises from it.

sentences.zh: 遺、補官秩雖卑，陛下侍臣也；

translations.literal: The Reminder and Supplementation Officers, though low in rank, are the emperor's attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The Reminder and Supplementation Officers, though low in rank, are the emperor's attendants;

sentences.zh: 中丞雖髙，法吏也。

translations.literal: the Imperial Censor, though high, is an officer of the law.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Censor, though high, is an officer of the law.

sentences.zh: 侍臣見淩，是不廣敬；

translations.literal: When attendants are trampled, respect is not broadly shown;
translations.idiomatic: When attendants are trampled, respect is not broadly shown;

sentences.zh: 法吏壞法，何以持繩？

translations.literal: when an officer of the law breaks the law, how can he hold the cord?
translations.idiomatic: when an officer of the law breaks the law, how can he hold the cord?

sentences.zh: 前時中書舍人李虞仲與造相逢，造乃曳去引馬。

translations.literal: Earlier when Secretariat Drafter Li Yuzhong met Zao, Zao dragged away the man leading his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Secretariat Drafter Li Yuzhong met Zao, Zao dragged away the man leading his horse.

sentences.zh: 知制誥崔咸與造相逢，造又捉其從人。

translations.literal: When Director of Imperial Edicts Cui Xian met Zao, Zao again seized his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of Imperial Edicts Cui Xian met Zao, Zao again seized his attendants.

sentences.zh: 當時縁不上聞，所以暴犯益甚。

translations.literal: At the time because it did not reach the throne, his violent offenses grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time because it did not reach the throne, his violent offenses grew worse.

sentences.zh: 臣聞元和、長慶中，中丞行李不過半坊，今乃遠至兩坊，謂之『籠街喝道』。

translations.literal: We have heard that in the Yuanhe and Changqing eras a censor's retinue did not pass half a ward; now it extends as far as two wards, called 'caging the street and shouting the way.'
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that in the Yuanhe and Changqing eras a censor's retinue did not pass half a ward; now it extends as far as two wards, called 'caging the street and shouting the way.'

sentences.zh: 但以崇髙自大，不思僭擬之嫌。

translations.literal: He merely exalts himself and does not consider the suspicion of overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: He merely exalts himself and does not consider the suspicion of overstepping.

sentences.zh: 若不糾繩，實虧彜典。」

translations.literal: If this is not corrected, it truly damages the constant statutes."
translations.idiomatic: If this is not corrected, it truly damages the constant statutes."

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「憲官之職，在指佞觸邪，不在行李自大；

translations.literal: The edict read, "The censor's duty lies in pointing out flattery and striking down evil—not in making one's retinue grand;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "The censor's duty lies in pointing out flattery and striking down evil—not in making one's retinue grand;

sentences.zh: 侍臣之職，在獻可替否，不在道路相髙。

translations.literal: the attendant's duty lies in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not—not in competing for precedence in the road.
translations.idiomatic: the attendant's duty lies in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not—not in competing for precedence in the road.

sentences.zh: 並列通班，合知名分，如聞喧競，亦已再三，既招人言，甚損朝體。

translations.literal: All stand in the same court ranks and should know their places; as we hear of these quarrels, they have already happened again and again, inviting talk and greatly harming court dignity.
translations.idiomatic: All stand in the same court ranks and should know their places. As we hear of these quarrels, they have already happened again and again, inviting talk and greatly harming court dignity.

sentences.zh: 其臺官與供奉官同道，聽先後而行，道途即祗揖而過，其參從人則各隨本官之後，少相辟避，勿言沖突。

translations.literal: When censorial officials and palace attendants share the same road, let them go first or last as they will; on the road let them bow and pass, while their attendants follow each behind his own master, yielding slightly and not speaking of collision.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial officials and palace attendants share the same road, let them go first or last as they will. On the road let them bow and pass, while their attendants follow each behind his own master, yielding slightly and not speaking of collision.

sentences.zh: 又聞近日已來，應合導從官，事力多者，街衢之中，行李太過。

translations.literal: We have also heard that recently, among officials who should have escorts, those with greater manpower make their retinues in the streets too large.
translations.idiomatic: We have also heard that recently, among officials who should have escorts, those with greater manpower make their retinues in the streets too large.

sentences.zh: 自今後，傳呼前後，不得過三百歩。」

translations.literal: From this day forward, before and behind the herald's call, no more than three hundred paces."
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, before and behind the herald's call, no more than three hundred paces."

sentences.zh: 然造之舉奏，無所吐茹。

translations.literal: Yet in Zao's impeachments he never held back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Zao's impeachments he never held back.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有喪不以禮、配不以類者，悉劾之。

translations.literal: Whenever at court there was mourning not according to ritual or matching not according to category, he impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever at court there was mourning not according to ritual or matching not according to category, he impeached them all.

sentences.zh: 獲偽官王果等九十餘人，杖殺南曹吏李賨等六人，刑於都市。

translations.literal: He seized more than ninety false officials such as Wang Guo and had six Southern Bureau clerks including Li Bin beaten to death, executing them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He seized more than ninety false officials such as Wang Guo and had six Southern Bureau clerks including Li Bin beaten to death, executing them in the market.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，加大中大夫，封祁縣開國子，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, given the additional title Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Viscount of Qi County, and granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, given the additional title Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Viscount of Qi County, and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 四年，興元軍亂，殺節度使李絳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Xingyuan army mutinied and killed Military Commissioner Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Xingyuan army mutinied and killed Military Commissioner Li Jue.

sentences.zh: 文宗以造氣豪嫉惡，乃授檢校右散騎常侍、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because Zao was bold, jealous of evil, and fierce, appointed him Acting Right Regular Palace Attendant, metropolitan magistrate of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, because Zao was bold, jealous of evil, and fierce, appointed him Acting Right Regular Palace Attendant, metropolitan magistrate of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 造辭赴鎭，以興元兆亂之狀奏之，文宗盡悟其根本，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Zao set out for his command he submitted the circumstances of Xingyuan's impending disorder; Wenzong fully grasped its root and permitted him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao set out for his command he submitted the circumstances of Xingyuan's impending disorder. Wenzong fully grasped its root and permitted him to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 帝慮用兵勞費，造奏曰：「臣計諸道征蠻之兵已回，俟臣行程至褒縣，望賜臣密詔，使受約束。

translations.literal: The emperor feared the labor and expense of using troops; Zao submitted, "By my reckoning the armies from the various circuits sent against the barbarians have already returned. When my journey reaches Bao County, I hope Your Majesty will grant me a secret edict so that I may receive their constraint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the labor and expense of using troops. Zao submitted, "By my reckoning the armies from the various circuits sent against the barbarians have already returned. When my journey reaches Bao County, I hope Your Majesty will grant me a secret edict so that I may receive their constraint.

sentences.zh: 比臣及興元，諸軍相續而至，臣用此足矣。」

translations.literal: By the time I reach Xingyuan the armies will arrive in succession—this will be enough for me."
translations.idiomatic: By the time I reach Xingyuan the armies will arrive in succession—this will be enough for me."

sentences.zh: 乃授造手詔四通。

translations.literal: He was therefore given four handwritten edicts from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given four handwritten edicts from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 神策行營將董重質、河中都將温德彜、郃陽都將劉士和等，咸令稟造之命。

translations.literal: The Shence field generals Dong Chongzhi, Hedong commander Wen Deyi, and Heyang commander Liu Shihe were all ordered to obey Zao's command.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence field generals Dong Chongzhi, Hedong commander Wen Deyi, and Heyang commander Liu Shihe were all ordered to obey Zao's command.

sentences.zh: 造行至褒城，會興元都將衞志忠征蠻回，謁見。

translations.literal: When Zao reached Bao City, Xingyuan commander Wei Zhizhong, returning from the barbarian campaign, came to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao reached Bao City, Xingyuan commander Wei Zhizhong, returning from the barbarian campaign, came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 造即留以自衞，密與志忠謀。

translations.literal: Zao immediately kept him as his own guard and secretly plotted with Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zao immediately kept him as his own guard and secretly plotted with Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 又召亞將張丕、李少直各諭其旨。

translations.literal: He also summoned sub-commanders Zhang Pi and Li Shaozhi and explained his intent to each.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned sub-commanders Zhang Pi and Li Shaozhi and explained his intent to each.

sentences.zh: 暨發褒城，以八百人爲衙隊，五百人爲前軍，入府分守諸門。

translations.literal: When they set out from Bao City, eight hundred men formed the headquarters guard and five hundred the vanguard; entering the headquarters they garrisoned each gate.
translations.idiomatic: When they set out from Bao City, eight hundred men formed the headquarters guard and five hundred the vanguard. Entering the headquarters they garrisoned each gate.

sentences.zh: 造下車置宴，所司供帳於廳事。

translations.literal: When Zao descended from his carriage a banquet was set; the offices prepared the tent in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao descended from his carriage a banquet was set. The offices prepared the tent in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 造曰：「此隘狹，不足以饗士卒，移之牙門。」

translations.literal: Zao said, "This is too cramped to feast the soldiers—move it to the headquarters gate."
translations.idiomatic: Zao said, "This is too cramped to feast the soldiers—move it to the headquarters gate."

sentences.zh: 坐定，將卒羅拜，志忠兵周環之。

translations.literal: Once seated, the officers and soldiers bowed in ranks, with Zhizhong's troops encircling them.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, the officers and soldiers bowed in ranks, with Zhizhong's troops encircling them.

sentences.zh: 造曰：「吾欲問新軍去住之意。

translations.literal: Zao said, "I wish to ask the new army's intent to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Zao said, "I wish to ask the new army's intent to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 可悉前，舊軍無得錯雜。」

translations.literal: Let all come forward; the old army must not mix in."
translations.idiomatic: Let all come forward; the old army must not mix in."

sentences.zh: 勞問既畢，傳言令坐，有未至者，因令舁酒巡行。

translations.literal: After the greetings were finished, word was passed to sit; those who had not yet arrived were told to carry wine and circulate.
translations.idiomatic: After the greetings were finished, word was passed to sit. Those who had not yet arrived were told to carry wine and circulate.

sentences.zh: 及酒匝，未至者皆至，牙兵圍之亦合。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone round, those who had not come all came, and the headquarters troops closed the ring as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone round, those who had not come all came, and the headquarters troops closed the ring as well.

sentences.zh: 坐卒未悟，席上有先覺者，揮令起，造傳言叱之，因帖息不敢動。

translations.literal: The seated soldiers had not yet understood; some who sensed it first on the mats waved to rise, but Zao passed word to shout them down, and they posted themselves and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: The seated soldiers had not yet understood. Some who sensed it first on the mats waved to rise, but Zao passed word to shout them down, and they posted themselves and dared not move.

sentences.zh: 即召坐卒，詰以殺絳之狀。

translations.literal: He then summoned the seated soldiers and interrogated them on the killing of Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the seated soldiers and interrogated them on the killing of Jue.

sentences.zh: 志忠、張丕夾階立，拔劍呼曰「殺」。

translations.literal: Zhizhong and Zhang Pi stood flanking the steps, drew their swords, and shouted "Kill!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong and Zhang Pi stood flanking the steps, drew their swords, and shouted, "Kill!"

sentences.zh: 圍兵齊奮，其賊首教練使丘鑄等並官健千人，皆斬首於地，血流四註。

translations.literal: The encircling troops charged together; the ringleaders, training commissioner Qiu Zhuo, and a thousand officers and soldiers were all beheaded on the ground, and blood flowed in four streams.
translations.idiomatic: The encircling troops charged together. The ringleaders, training commissioner Qiu Zhuo, and a thousand officers and soldiers were all beheaded on the ground, and blood flowed in four streams.

sentences.zh: 監軍楊叔元在座，遽起求哀，擁造靴以請命；

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Yang Shuyuan was among those seated; he sprang up to beg for mercy and clutched Zao's boots to plead for his life;
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Yang Shuyuan was among those seated. He sprang up to beg for mercy and clutched Zao's boots to plead for his life;

sentences.zh: 遣兵衞出之，以俟朝旨。

translations.literal: Zao sent troops to escort him out and await the court's decree.
translations.idiomatic: Zao sent troops to escort him out and await the court's decree.

sentences.zh: 敕旨配流康州。

translations.literal: An imperial edict banished him to Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict banished him to Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其親刃絳者斬一百斷，號令者斬三斷，餘並斬首。

translations.literal: Those who personally struck Jue were cut in one hundred segments, those who gave the orders in three segments, and the rest were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Those who personally struck Jue were cut in one hundred segments, those who gave the orders in three segments, and the rest were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 内一百首祭李絳，三十首祭王景延、趙存約等，並投屍於江。

translations.literal: One hundred heads were offered in sacrifice to Li Jue, thirty to Wang Jingyan, Zhao Cunyue, and others, and the corpses were all cast into the river.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred heads were offered in sacrifice to Li Jue, thirty to Wang Jingyan, Zhao Cunyue, and others, and the corpses were all cast into the river.

sentences.zh: 以功就加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was promptly promoted to acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promptly made acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，入爲兵部侍郎，以耳疾求退。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year he entered the capital as Vice Minister of War and, because of an ear ailment, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year he returned to the capital as Vice Minister of War and asked to retire on account of an ear ailment.

sentences.zh: 七月，檢校戸部尚書、東都留守，判東都尚書省事、東畿汝防禦使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was made acting Minister of Revenue and Eastern Capital Protector, with charge of the Eastern Capital Secretariat and duty as defense commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan Region and Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was named acting Minister of Revenue and Eastern Capital Protector, with charge of the Eastern Capital Secretariat and duty as defense commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan Region and Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 造至洛中。

translations.literal: Zao arrived at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zao reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，制改授河陽懷節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict transferred him to serve as military commissioner and circuit supervisor of Heyang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict reassigned him as military commissioner and circuit supervisor of Heyang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 造以河内膏腴，民戸雕瘵，奏開浚懷州古秦渠枋口堰；

translations.literal: Zao, because the lands within the river were fertile yet the households were wasted and impoverished, memorialized to open and dredge the ancient Qin Canal weir at Fangkou in Huai Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Finding the lands within the river fertile yet the people wasted and impoverished, Zao memorialized to open and dredge the ancient Qin Canal weir at Fangkou in Huai Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 役工四萬，溉濟源、河内、温、武陟四縣田五千餘頃。

translations.literal: employing forty thousand laborers, it irrigated more than five thousand mou of fields in the four counties of Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand workers were employed, irrigating more than five thousand mou of farmland in Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月，入爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he returned to the capital as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 造初赴鎭漢中，遇大雨，平地水深尺餘，乃禱鷄翁山祈晴，俄而疾風驅雲，即時開齊。

translations.literal: When Zao first went to his post at Hanzhong, he encountered heavy rain; the flat ground was more than a foot deep in water. He therefore prayed at Cock-Old-Man Mountain for clear skies, and soon a fierce wind drove off the clouds and the sky immediately cleared.
translations.idiomatic: On his first journey to his post at Hanzhong, Zao was caught in heavy rain that left the flat ground more than a foot underwater. He prayed at Cock-Old-Man Mountain for clear weather, and soon a fierce wind drove off the clouds and the skies opened.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗聞其事，會造入對言之，乃詔封鷄翁山爲侯。

translations.literal: Wenzong had heard of this matter; when Zao entered for audience and spoke of it, an edict was issued ennobling Cock-Old-Man Mountain as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong had heard of the incident; when Zao mentioned it during an audience, the emperor issued an edict ennobling Cock-Old-Man Mountain as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其年六月病卒，時年七十，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year he died of illness, at age seventy; posthumously given the title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness that sixth month, at the age of seventy, and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有文集八十巻。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in eighty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in eighty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 造於晩年積聚財貨，一無散施，時頗譏之。

translations.literal: In his later years Zao amassed wealth and goods but gave nothing away; people at the time frequently ridiculed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Zao amassed wealth but gave nothing away, and many at the time mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 子璋嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 璋以廕入仕，累佐使府，歴三郡刺史。

translations.literal: Zhang entered service through hereditary privilege, served repeatedly on military commissioners' staffs, and held three successive prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang entered government through hereditary privilege, served repeatedly on commissioners' staffs, and governed three prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，爲徐泗節度使，徐州牙卒曰銀刀軍，頗驕橫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantong reign he became military commissioner of Xu and Si; the Xu Prefecture guards were called the Silver Blade Army and were quite arrogant and domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xiantong reign he became military commissioner of Xu and Si, where the Xu Prefecture guards—the Silver Blade Army—were notoriously arrogant and domineering.

sentences.zh: 璋至，誅其惡者五百餘人，自是軍中畏法。

translations.literal: When Zhang arrived, he executed more than five hundred of the worst offenders; from then on the army feared the law.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Zhang executed more than five hundred of the worst offenders, and thereafter the army feared the law.

sentences.zh: 入爲京兆尹，持法太深，豪右一皆屛跡。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao; his enforcement of the law was too severe, and the great families all vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, where his stern enforcement of the law drove every powerful family into hiding.

sentences.zh: 會同昌公主薨，懿宗怒，殺醫官，其家屬宗枝下獄者三百人。

translations.literal: It happened that Princess Tongchang died; Yizong was enraged and executed the physicians; three hundred of their kinsmen and clansmen were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Tongchang died, Yizong in his rage executed the physicians and imprisoned three hundred of their kinsmen and clansmen.

sentences.zh: 璋上疎切諫，以爲刑法太深。

translations.literal: Zhang submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, holding that the penal law was too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang submitted a forceful memorial arguing that the punishments were too harsh.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶璋振州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Zhang to staff administrator of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor demoted Zhang to staff administrator of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 制出，璋嘆曰：「生不逢時，死何足惜？」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Zhang sighed: "Born out of season—what is death worth regretting?"
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Zhang sighed, "Born out of season—why regret death?"

sentences.zh: 是夜自縊而卒。

translations.literal: That night he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 郭承嘏，字復卿。

translations.literal: Guo Chenggu, styled Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chenggu, styled Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖尚父汾陽王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was the Prince of Fenyang, the Lord Father of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was the Prince of Fenyang, the Lord Father of the State.

sentences.zh: 祖晞，諸衞將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was a general of the imperial guards.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi was a general of the imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 父鈞。

translations.literal: His father Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jun.

sentences.zh: 承嘏生而秀異，乳保之年，即好筆硯。

translations.literal: Chenggu was gifted and exceptional from birth; even in the years of his wet nurse he loved brush and inkstone.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggu was gifted from birth; even as a nursling he loved brush and inkstone.

sentences.zh: 比及成童，能通《五經》。

translations.literal: By the time he reached boyhood he had mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: By boyhood he had mastered the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，禮部侍郎張弘靖知其才，擢升進士第，累辟使幕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Yuanhe reign, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Hongjing recognized his talent and advanced him to the jinshi degree; he was repeatedly recruited to commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Hongjing recognized his talent and advanced him to the jinshi degree; he served repeatedly on commissioners' staffs.

sentences.zh: 歴渭南尉。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 入朝爲監察御史，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court as investigating censor and was promoted to recorder of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as investigating censor and was promoted to recorder of conduct.

sentences.zh: 丁内艱，以孝聞，終喪，爲侍御史，職方、兵部二員外，兵部郎中。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he was known for filial piety; after the mourning period ended he became attendant censor, then successively vice director in the Ministries of Appointments and War, and director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he was known for filial piety; after the mourning period he became attendant censor, then successively vice director in the Ministries of Appointments and War, and director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Taihe reign he was appointed Remonstrance and Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe he was appointed Remonstrance and Reviser.

sentences.zh: 頻上疎，言時政得失。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials discussing the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on the strengths and failings of current policy.

sentences.zh: 文宗以鄭註爲太仆卿，承嘏論諫激切，註甚懼之。

translations.literal: When Wenzong appointed Zheng Zhu Director of the Imperial Stud, Chenggu remonstrated with fierce urgency, and Zhu was greatly afraid of him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong appointed Zheng Zhu Director of the Imperial Stud, Chenggu remonstrated with fierce urgency, and Zhu was greatly afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 本官知匭院事。

translations.literal: In his regular post he also managed affairs of the Petition Box.
translations.idiomatic: In his regular post he also managed affairs of the Petition Box.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，出爲華州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he went out as prefect of Hua and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng he was appointed prefect of Hua and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 詔下，兩省叠詣中書，求承嘏出麾之由。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, members of the two bureaus went repeatedly to the Secretariat to ask the reason for Chenggu's assignment outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, members of the two bureaus went repeatedly to the Secretariat to ask why Chenggu was being sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧載封還詔書，奏曰：「承嘏自居此官，繼有封駁，能奉其職，宜在瑣闥。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Lu Zai returned the sealed edict and memorialized: "Since Chenggu has held this office he has repeatedly drafted rejections and can fulfill his duties; he should remain in the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Zai returned the sealed edict and memorialized, "Since Chenggu has held this office he has repeatedly drafted rejections and fulfilled his duties well; he should remain at court.

sentences.zh: 牧守之才，易爲推擇。」

translations.literal: The talent of a prefect is easy to find elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: A capable prefect is easy enough to find."

sentences.zh: 文宗謂宰臣曰：「承嘏久在黃扉，欲優其祿俸，暫令廉問近關。

translations.literal: Wenzong told the chancellors: "Chenggu has long served in the yellow gate; I wished to improve his salary and briefly sent him to inspect a nearby pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong told the chancellors, "Chenggu has long served at court; I wished to improve his salary and briefly sent him to inspect a nearby pass.

sentences.zh: 而諫列拜章，惜其稱職，甚美事也。」

translations.literal: Yet the remonstrance officials submitted memorials, cherishing his competence in office—a very fine thing indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the remonstrance officials submitted memorials, valuing his competence in office—a very fine thing indeed."

sentences.zh: 乃復爲給事中。

translations.literal: He was then restored to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was then restored to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 文宗以淮南諸道累歳大旱，租賦不登，國用多闕。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because the circuits south of the Huai had suffered great drought for successive years and taxes and levies had not been collected, found state revenues greatly short.
translations.idiomatic: Because the circuits south of the Huai had suffered great drought for successive years and taxes had gone uncollected, Wenzong found state revenues greatly short.

sentences.zh: 及是，以度支、戸部分命宰臣鎭之。

translations.literal: At this time the ministries of revenue and household accounts were entrusted to chancellors to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the ministries of revenue and household accounts were entrusted to chancellors to supervise.

sentences.zh: 承嘏論之曰：「宰相者，上調陰陽，下安黎庶，致君堯、舜，致時淸平。

translations.literal: Chenggu argued: "Chancellors should harmonize yin and yang above and settle the common people below, bring the ruler to the level of Yao and Shun, and bring the age to clarity and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggu argued, "Chancellors should harmonize yin and yang above and settle the common people below, bring the ruler to the level of Yao and Shun, and bring the age to clarity and peace.

sentences.zh: 俾之閲簿書，算緡帛，非所宜也。」

translations.literal: To have them examine ledgers and calculate strings of cash is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: To have them examine ledgers and count strings of cash is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved and promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved and promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時因朔望，以刑法官得對，文宗從容顧問，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time, on the first and fifteenth of each month, judicial officials were permitted audience; Wenzong questioned him at leisure, and his favor and courtesy were very great.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, on the first and fifteenth of each month, judicial officials were permitted audience; Wenzong questioned him at leisure, and his favor and courtesy were very great.

sentences.zh: 未及大用，以二年二月卒。

translations.literal: Before he could be greatly employed, he died in the second month of the second year.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could be greatly employed, he died in the second month of the second year.

sentences.zh: 承嘏身歿之後，家無餘財，喪祭所費，皆親友共給而後具。

translations.literal: After Chenggu's death his household had no surplus wealth; the expenses of burial and sacrifice were all supplied by relatives and friends before they could be completed.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenggu's death his household had no surplus wealth; burial and sacrifice expenses were all supplied by relatives and friends before they could be completed.

sentences.zh: 搢紳之流，無不痛惜。

translations.literal: Among the gentry there was none who did not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 殷侑，陳郡人。

translations.literal: Yin You, a man of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You was a man of Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父懌。

translations.literal: His father Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yi.

sentences.zh: 侑爲兒童時，勵志力學，不問家人資産。

translations.literal: As a child You was determined to study hard and paid no heed to his family's property.
translations.idiomatic: As a child You was determined to study hard and paid no heed to his family's property.

sentences.zh: 及長，通經，以講習自娯。

translations.literal: When he grew up he mastered the classics and took lecturing and study as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he mastered the classics and took lecturing and study as his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，以《五經》登第，精於歴代沿革禮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan reign he passed the examination in the Five Classics and was expert in the rites and institutions of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenyuan he passed the examination in the Five Classics and was expert in the rites and institutions of successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 元和中，累爲太常博士。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe reign he served repeatedly as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe he served repeatedly as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時回紇請和親，朝廷計費五百萬緡。

translations.literal: At that time the Uighurs requested a marriage alliance, and the court calculated the cost at five million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Uighurs requested a marriage alliance, and the court calculated the cost at five million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方用兵伐叛，費用百端，欲緩其期。

translations.literal: The court was then campaigning against rebels and expenses were manifold; it wished to delay the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against rebels and expenses were manifold; it wished to delay the matter.

sentences.zh: 乃命宗正少卿李孝誠奉使宣諭，以侑爲副。

translations.literal: It therefore appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Li Xiaocheng to go as envoy to announce and instruct, with You as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: It therefore appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Li Xiaocheng to go as envoy to announce and instruct, with You as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 侑謹重有節概，臨事俊辯。

translations.literal: You was careful, weighty, and possessed of integrity; in handling affairs he was sharp and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: You was careful, weighty, and possessed of integrity; in handling affairs he was sharp and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 既至虜庭，可汗初待漢使，盛陳兵甲，欲臣漢使而不答拜。

translations.literal: Once they reached the barbarian court, the khan at first received the Han envoys with a great display of arms and armor, intending to make the Han envoys bow without receiving their return bow.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached the khan's court, the khan at first received the Han envoys with a great display of arms and armor, intending to make them bow without returning the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 侑堅立不動，宣諭畢，可汗責其倨，宣言欲留而不遣。

translations.literal: You stood firm without moving; when the announcement was finished the khan reproached his arrogance and declared he intended to detain them and not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: You stood firm without moving; when the announcement was finished the khan reproached his arrogance and declared he intended to detain them and not send them back.

sentences.zh: 行者皆懼，侑謂虜使曰：「可汗是漢家子婿，欲坐受使臣拜，是可汗失禮，非使臣之倨也。」

translations.literal: The travelers were all afraid; You told the barbarian envoy: "The khan is the Han emperor's son-in-law; if he wishes to sit and receive the envoy's bow, it is the khan who has lost propriety, not the envoy's arrogance."
translations.idiomatic: The travelers were all afraid; You told the barbarian envoy, "The khan is the Han emperor's son-in-law; if he wishes to sit and receive the envoy's bow, it is the khan who has lost propriety, not the envoy's arrogance."

sentences.zh: 可汗憚其言，卒不敢逼。

translations.literal: The khan feared his words and in the end did not dare compel him.
translations.idiomatic: The khan feared his words and in the end did not dare compel him.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: On returning from the mission he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Parks.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the mission he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Parks.

sentences.zh: 王承宗拒命，遣侑銜命招諭之。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong defied orders; You was sent bearing imperial command to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong defied orders; You was sent bearing imperial command to summon and instruct him.

sentences.zh: 承宗尋稟朝旨，獻德、棣二州，遣二子入朝。

translations.literal: Chengzong soon submitted to court instructions, presented De and Di prefectures, and sent two sons to court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong soon submitted to court instructions, presented De and Di prefectures, and sent two sons to court.

sentences.zh: 遷侑諫議大夫。

translations.literal: You was promoted to Remonstrance and Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: You was promoted to Remonstrance and Reviser.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷之得失，悉以陳論。

translations.literal: Whatever gains or losses the court suffered, he set them all forth in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever gains or losses the court suffered, he set them all forth in discussion.

sentences.zh: 前後上八十四章，以言激切，出爲桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: In all he submitted eighty-four memorials; because his words were fierce and urgent he was sent out as supervisory commissioner of the Gui circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In all he submitted eighty-four memorials; because his words were fierce and urgent he was sent out as supervisory commissioner of the Gui circuit.

sentences.zh: 寶暦元年，檢校右散騎常侍、洪州刺史，轉江西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he was made acting Right Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Hong, then transferred to supervisory commissioner of the Jiangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he was made acting Right Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Hong, then transferred to supervisory commissioner of the Jiangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 所至以潔廉著稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he was known for purity and integrity.

sentences.zh: 入爲衞尉卿。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 文宗初即位，滄州李同捷叛，而王廷湊助逆，欲加兵鎭州，詔五品已上都省集議。

translations.literal: When Wenzong first took the throne, Li Tongjie of Cang Prefecture rebelled while Wang Tingcou aided the rebellion; the court wished to send troops against Zhen Prefecture and ordered all officials of the fifth rank and above in the central ministries to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong first took the throne, Li Tongjie of Cang Prefecture rebelled while Wang Tingcou aided the rebellion; the court wished to send troops against Zhen Prefecture and ordered all officials of the fifth rank and above in the central ministries to assemble for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時上鋭於破賊，宰臣莫敢異議。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was eager to crush the rebels, and no chancellor dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was eager to crush the rebels, and no chancellor dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 獨侑以廷湊再亂河朔，方徇招懷，雖附兇徒，未甚彰露，宜且含容，專討同捷。

translations.literal: Only You held that Tingcou had twice thrown the Hebei region into turmoil; the court was then pursuing appeasement, and though he had joined the violent faction his offense was not yet fully exposed—he should for the time being be tolerated while the court concentrated on Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Only You held that Tingcou had twice thrown the Hebei region into turmoil; the court was then pursuing appeasement, and though he had joined the violent faction his offense was not yet fully exposed—he should for the time being be tolerated while the court concentrated on Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 其疎末云：「伏願以宗社安危爲大計，以善師攻心爲神武，以含垢安人爲遠圖，以網漏呑舟爲至誡。」

translations.literal: At the end of his memorial he wrote: "I humbly hope Your Majesty will take the security of the altars of state as the great plan, take winning hearts by a good army as divine martial prowess, take bearing grime to settle the people as far-reaching design, and take letting the net leak so great boats pass as the highest caution."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his memorial he wrote, "I humbly hope Your Majesty will take the security of the altars of state as the great plan, take winning hearts by a good army as divine martial prowess, take bearing grime to settle the people as far-reaching design, and take letting the net leak so great boats pass as the highest caution."

sentences.zh: 文宗雖不納，深所嘉之。

translations.literal: Wenzong did not adopt it, but greatly approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong did not adopt it, but greatly approved of it.

sentences.zh: 滄景平，以侑嘗爲滄州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Cang and Jing were pacified, because You had once served as acting military administrator of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Cang and Jing were pacified, because You had once served as acting military administrator of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，加檢校工部尚書、滄齊德觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was made acting Minister of Works and supervisory commissioner of the Cang, Qi, and De circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was made acting Minister of Works and supervisory commissioner of the Cang, Qi, and De circuit.

sentences.zh: 時大兵之後，滿目荊榛，遺骸蔽野，寂無人煙。

translations.literal: At that time, after great military campaigns, thorns and brambles filled the eye everywhere, abandoned corpses covered the wilds, and there was silence with no human smoke.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after great military campaigns, thorns and brambles filled the landscape, abandoned corpses covered the wilds, and the land lay silent and deserted.

sentences.zh: 侑不以妻子之官，始至，空城而已。

translations.literal: You did not bring his wife and children to his post; when he first arrived there was only an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: You did not bring his wife and children to his post; when he first arrived there was only an empty city.

sentences.zh: 侑攻苦食淡，與士卒同勞苦。

translations.literal: You ate sparingly and labored bitterly, sharing hardship with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: You ate sparingly and labored bitterly, sharing hardship with the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 周歳之後，流民繈負而歸。

translations.literal: After a full year, displaced people returned carrying their children on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year, displaced people returned carrying their children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 侑上表請借耕牛三萬，以給流民，乃詔度支賜綾絹五萬匹，買牛以給之。

translations.literal: You submitted a memorial requesting to borrow thirty thousand plow oxen to supply the displaced people; an edict was then issued for the Ministry of Revenue to grant fifty thousand bolts of silk and damask to buy oxen and distribute them.
translations.idiomatic: You submitted a memorial requesting to borrow thirty thousand plow oxen to supply the displaced people; an edict was then issued for the Ministry of Revenue to grant fifty thousand bolts of silk and damask to buy oxen and distribute them.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，戸口滋饒，倉稟盈積，人皆忘亡。

translations.literal: After several years households multiplied and storehouses overflowed; people forgot exile and death.
translations.idiomatic: After several years households multiplied and storehouses overflowed; people forgot exile and death.

sentences.zh: 初州兵三萬，悉取給於度支。

translations.literal: At first the prefectural army numbered thirty thousand, all supplied by the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefectural army numbered thirty thousand, all supplied by the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 侑一歳而賦入自贍其半，二歳而給用悉周，請罷度支給賜。

translations.literal: In one year You's tax revenues supported half of them; in two years supplies were fully covered, and he requested that Ministry of Revenue grants be ended.
translations.idiomatic: In one year You's tax revenues supported half of them; in two years supplies were fully covered, and he requested that Ministry of Revenue grants be ended.

sentences.zh: 而勸課多方，民吏胥悅，上表請立德政碑。

translations.literal: He also encouraged agriculture in many ways; officials and clerks were all pleased, and he submitted a memorial requesting a stele of virtuous governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also encouraged agriculture in many ways; officials and clerks were all pleased, and he submitted a memorial requesting a stele of virtuous governance.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was made acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievement he was made acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 侑以郭下淸池縣在子城北，非便，奏移於南郭之内。

translations.literal: You held that Qingchi County under the prefectural seat lay north of the inner city and was inconvenient; he memorialized to move it within the southern wall.
translations.idiomatic: You held that Qingchi County under the prefectural seat lay north of the inner city and was inconvenient; he memorialized to move it within the southern wall.

sentences.zh: 六年，入爲刑部尚書，尋復檢校吏部尚書、鄆州刺史、兼御史大夫，充天平軍節度、鄆曹濮觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered [the capital] as Minister of Justice, then again became acting Minister of Personnel, prefect of Yan, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as military commissioner of the Tianping Army and supervisory commissioner of Yan, Cao, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to the capital as Minister of Justice, then again became acting Minister of Personnel, prefect of Yan, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as military commissioner of the Tianping Army and supervisory commissioner of Yan, Cao, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 自元和末，收復師道十二州爲三鎭。

translations.literal: From the end of the Yuanhe reign, when the twelve prefectures of Shidao were recovered they became three commands.
translations.idiomatic: From the end of Yuanhe, when the twelve prefectures of Shidao were recovered they became three commands.

sentences.zh: 朝廷務安反側，征賦所入，盡留贍軍，貫緡尺帛，不入王府。

translations.literal: The court sought to settle those who had turned against it; all tax revenues collected were retained to support the army—strings of cash and bolts of cloth and silk did not enter the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought to settle those who had turned against it; all tax revenues collected were retained to support the army—strings of cash and bolts of cloth and silk did not enter the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 侑以軍賦有餘，賦不上供，非法也，乃上表起太和七年，請歳供兩稅、榷酒等錢十五萬貫、粟五萬碩。

translations.literal: You held that since military levies had a surplus and taxes were not submitted upward, this was unlawful; he therefore submitted a memorial beginning with the seventh year of Taihe, requesting annual submission of fifteen thousand strings of the two taxes and monopoly wine revenues, and fifty thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: You held that since military levies had a surplus and taxes were not submitted upward, this was unlawful; he therefore submitted a memorial beginning with the seventh year of Taihe, requesting annual submission of fifteen thousand strings of the two taxes and monopoly wine revenues, and fifty thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「鄆、曹、濮等州，元和已來，地本殷實，自分三道，十五餘年，雖頒詔書，竟未入賦。

translations.literal: An edict read: "The prefectures of Yan, Cao, and Pu, since the Yuanhe reign, were originally prosperous lands; since they were divided into three commands, more than fifteen years have passed; though edicts were repeatedly issued, taxes were never submitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "The prefectures of Yan, Cao, and Pu, since Yuanhe, were originally prosperous lands; since they were divided into three commands, more than fifteen years have passed; though edicts were repeatedly issued, taxes were never submitted.

sentences.zh: 殷侑承兵戈之後，當歉旱之餘，勤力奉公，謹身守法。

translations.literal: Yin You, after the warfare, amid famine and drought, labored diligently in service to the state and kept himself careful and law-abiding.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You, after the warfare, amid famine and drought, labored diligently in service to the state and kept himself careful and law-abiding.

sentences.zh: 才及周歳，已致阜安。

translations.literal: In barely a full year he already brought prosperity and peace.
translations.idiomatic: In barely a full year he already brought prosperity and peace.

sentences.zh: 而又體國輸忠，率先入貢，成三軍奉上之志，陳一境樂輸之心。

translations.literal: Moreover he embodied the state's loyalty, took the lead in submitting tribute, fulfilled the three armies' intent to serve the throne, and expressed the whole circuit's willingness to contribute.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he embodied the state's loyalty, took the lead in submitting tribute, fulfilled the three armies' intent to serve the throne, and expressed the whole circuit's willingness to contribute.

sentences.zh: 尋有表章，良用嘉嘆！」

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted another memorial—truly worthy of praise and admiration!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he submitted another memorial—truly worthy of praise and admiration!"

sentences.zh: 尋就加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: He was then promptly made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promptly made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年，御史大夫温造劾侑不由制旨，增監軍俸入，賦斂於人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao impeached You for increasing the army supervisor's salary income without following the prescribed edict and levying taxes on the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao impeached You for increasing the army supervisor's salary income without following the prescribed edict and levying taxes on the people.

sentences.zh: 上不問，以庾承宣代還。

translations.literal: The emperor did not inquire into it and sent Yu Chengxuan to replace him and return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not inquire into it and sent Yu Chengxuan to replace him and return.

sentences.zh: 其年，濮州録事參軍崔元武，於五縣人吏率斂，及縣官料錢，以私馬擡估納官，計絹一百二十匹。

translations.literal: That year, Pu Prefecture recorder Cui Yuanwu, among the clerks and officials of five counties, collected levies and official stipend money, used a private horse to inflate the valuation and submit it to the government, totaling one hundred twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Pu Prefecture recorder Cui Yuanwu, among the clerks and officials of five counties, collected levies and official stipend money, used a private horse to inflate the valuation and submit it to the government, totaling one hundred twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 大理寺斷三犯倶發，以重者論。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review ruled on three offenses committed together and judged by the most serious.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review ruled on three offenses committed together and judged by the most serious.

sentences.zh: 只以中私馬爲重，止令削三任官。

translations.literal: They took only the private horse offense as the serious one and merely ordered removal from three ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: They took only the private horse offense as the serious one and merely ordered removal from three ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 而刑部覆奏，令決杖配流。

translations.literal: But the Ministry of Justice on review memorialized ordering beating with the staff and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: But the Ministry of Justice on review memorialized ordering beating with the staff and banishment.

sentences.zh: 獄未決。

translations.literal: The case was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The case was not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 侑奏曰：「法官不習法律，三犯不同，即坐其所重。

translations.literal: You memorialized: "The judges do not understand the law; when three offenses differ, they should be punished for the most serious.
translations.idiomatic: You memorialized, "The judges do not understand the law; when three offenses differ, they should be punished for the most serious.

sentences.zh: 元武所犯，皆枉法取受，準律，枉法十五匹已上絞。

translations.literal: All of Yuanwu's offenses were wrongful taking and receipt; according to the code, wrongful taking of fifteen bolts or more warrants strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: All of Yuanwu's offenses were wrongful taking and receipt; according to the code, wrongful taking of fifteen bolts or more warrants strangulation.

sentences.zh: 《律疎》云：即以贓致罪，頻犯者並累科。

translations.literal: The Statutes Commentary states: when crimes are caused by illicit goods and offenses are repeatedly committed, punishments are cumulated.
translations.idiomatic: The Statutes Commentary states: when crimes are caused by illicit goods and offenses are repeatedly committed, punishments are cumulated.

sentences.zh: 據元武所犯，令當入處絞刑。」

translations.literal: According to Yuanwu's offenses, he should receive strangulation."
translations.idiomatic: According to Yuanwu's offenses, he should receive strangulation."

sentences.zh: 疎奏，元武依刑部奏，決六十，流賀州。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yuanwu was decided according to the Ministry of Justice memorial: sixty blows with the staff and banishment to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Yuanwu was decided according to the Ministry of Justice memorial: sixty blows with the staff and banishment to He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乃授侑刑部尚書。

translations.literal: You was then appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: You was then appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 八月，檢校右僕射，復爲天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again became military commissioner of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again became military commissioner of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 上以温造所奏深文故也。

translations.literal: The emperor did this because of the harsh legalism in Wen Zao's impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did this because of the harsh legalism in Wen Zao's impeachment.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，復召爲刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時初經李訓之亂，上問侑治安之術。

translations.literal: At that time, having just passed through the turmoil of Li Xun, the emperor asked You about the art of securing peace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, having just passed through the turmoil of Li Xun, the emperor asked You about the art of securing peace.

sentences.zh: 侑極言委任責成，宜在朝之耆德，新進小生，無宜輕用。

translations.literal: You spoke forcefully of entrusting responsibility and demanding results; the court should rely on elders of virtue, and newly advanced young men should not be lightly employed.
translations.idiomatic: You spoke forcefully of entrusting responsibility and demanding results; the court should rely on elders of virtue, and newly advanced young men should not be lightly employed.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之，賜錦彩三百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 及中謝，又令中使就第賜金十斤。

translations.literal: At his audience of thanks he was again ordered by palace envoy to his residence to bestow ten jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of thanks he was again ordered by palace envoy to his residence to bestow ten jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，檢校左僕射，出爲襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as prefect of Xiang and military commissioner of the Shannan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as prefect of Xiang and military commissioner of the Shannan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，以病求代，以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he requested replacement on account of illness and was made Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he requested replacement on account of illness and was made Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復檢校右僕射，出爲忠武節度、陳許蔡觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was again made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as military commissioner of Zhongwu and supervisory commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was again made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as military commissioner of Zhongwu and supervisory commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，卒於鎭，時年七十二，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year he died at his post, at age seventy-two; posthumously given the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he died at his post, at age seventy-two, and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侑以通經入仕，觀風撫俗，所蒞有聲。

translations.literal: You entered service through mastery of the classics; in observing customs and settling the people, wherever he served he had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: You entered service through mastery of the classics; in observing customs and settling the people, wherever he served he had a reputation.

sentences.zh: 而晩年急於大用，稍通權幸，物望減於往時。

translations.literal: But in his later years he was eager for great employment and gradually cultivated connections with the powerful; public esteem fell short of earlier times.
translations.idiomatic: But in his later years he was eager for great employment and gradually cultivated connections with the powerful; public esteem fell short of earlier times.

sentences.zh: 子羽。

translations.literal: His son Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽太和五年登進士第，籓府辟召，不至通顯。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Taihe; he was recruited to commissioners' staffs but never rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Taihe; he was recruited to commissioners' staffs but never rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 子盈孫。

translations.literal: His son Yingsun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yingsun.

sentences.zh: 盈孫，乾符末爲成都掾。

translations.literal: Yingsun, at the end of the Qianfu reign, was an aide in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun, at the end of the Qianfu reign, was an aide in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 駕在西川，用爲太常博士，禮學有祖風。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in western Shu he was employed as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in ritual learning he had his family's style.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was in western Shu he was employed as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in ritual learning he had his family's style.

sentences.zh: 光啓二年冬，隨駕自成都還。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangqi he followed the emperor back from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Guangqi he followed the emperor back from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，駐蹕鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the imperial carriage halted at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year the imperial carriage halted at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 時宗廟爲賊所焚，車駕至京，告享無所。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial ancestral temple had been burned by rebels; when the imperial carriage reached the capital there was nowhere to announce the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial ancestral temple had been burned by rebels; when the imperial carriage reached the capital there was nowhere to announce the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 四月，盈孫謂宰執曰：「太廟十一室，並祧廟八室，及三太后三室，因光啓元年十二月二十五日車駕出宮，其縁室法物神主，本司載行，至鄠縣並被盜剽奪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Yingsun told the chief ministers: "The main temple has eleven chambers, together with eight chambers of the disestablished temple, and three chambers for the three empresses—a total of twenty-two. Because on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi, when the imperial carriage left the palace, the ritual objects and spirit tablets of those chambers that the office was to transport were all looted at Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yingsun told the chief ministers, "The main temple has eleven chambers, together with eight chambers of the disestablished temple, and three chambers for the three empresses—a total of twenty-two. Because on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi, when the imperial carriage left the palace, the ritual objects and spirit tablets of those chambers that the office was to transport were all looted at Hu County.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還宮，合先制造。」

translations.literal: Now that the emperor has returned to the palace, they should first be remade."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the emperor has returned to the palace, they should first be remade."

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭延昌奏曰：「太廟大殿二十二間，功績至大，計料支費不少；

translations.literal: Chancellor Zheng Yanchang memorialized: "The main hall of the imperial ancestral temple has twenty-two bays; the materials and expenses are very great;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zheng Yanchang memorialized, "The main hall of the imperial ancestral temple has twenty-two bays; the materials and expenses are very great;

sentences.zh: 兼宗廟制度，損益重難，今未審依元料修奉，爲復別有商量。」

translations.literal: and the temple institutions, whether to reduce or increase, are weighty and difficult. It is not yet clear whether to repair according to the original specifications or to deliberate otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: and the temple institutions, whether to reduce or increase, are weighty and difficult. It is not yet clear whether to repair according to the original specifications or to deliberate otherwise."

sentences.zh: 敕付禮院詳議。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict entrusted the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時博士四人，杜用勵在利州，崔澄在河中，封舜卿在巴南。

translations.literal: At that time there were four erudites: Du Yongli was in Li Prefecture, Cui Cheng in Hezhong, and Feng Shunqing in Banan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were four erudites: Du Yongli was in Li Prefecture, Cui Cheng in Hezhong, and Feng Shunqing in Banan.

sentences.zh: 獨盈孫獻議曰：「太廟制度。

translations.literal: Only Yingsun submitted an opinion: "On the institutions of the imperial ancestral temple,
translations.idiomatic: Only Yingsun submitted an opinion: "On the institutions of the imperial ancestral temple,

sentences.zh: 歴代參詳，皆符典經，難議損益。

translations.literal: successive dynasties have examined them in detail; all accord with canonical standards, and reduction or increase is difficult to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: successive dynasties have examined them in detail; all accord with canonical standards, and reduction or increase is difficult to discuss.

sentences.zh: 謹按舊制，十一室，二十三間，十一架。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the old institutions: eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, eleven frames.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the old institutions: eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, eleven frames.

sentences.zh: 垣墉廣袤之度，堂室淺深之規，階陛等級之差，棟宇崇低之則，前古所謂奢不能侈，儉不能逾者也。

translations.literal: The breadth and length of the enclosing walls, the depth and shallowness of the halls and chambers, the gradations of steps and stairs, the standards of height and loftiness of the beams and rafters—all these are what the ancients called that extravagance cannot exceed and frugality cannot fall below.
translations.idiomatic: The breadth and length of the enclosing walls, the depth and shallowness of the halls and chambers, the gradations of steps and stairs, the standards of height and loftiness of the beams and rafters—all these are what the ancients called that extravagance cannot exceed and frugality cannot fall below.

sentences.zh: 今以朝廷帑藏方虚，費用稍廣，須資變禮，將務從宜，固不可易前聖之規模，狹大朝之制度，當憑典實，別有參詳。

translations.literal: Now the court treasury is empty and expenses somewhat broad; we must rely on altered rites and strive for what is fitting—but we cannot change the former sage's scale or narrow the great court's institutions; we should rely on canonical fact and deliberate separately.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court treasury is empty and expenses somewhat broad; we must rely on altered rites and strive for what is fitting—but we cannot change the former sage's scale or narrow the great court's institutions; we should rely on canonical fact and deliberate separately.

sentences.zh: 謹按至德二年，以太廟方修，新作神主，於長安殿安置，便行饗告之禮，如同宗廟之儀，以俟廟成，方爲遷祔。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that in the second year of Zhide, because the imperial ancestral temple was under repair, new spirit tablets were made and placed in Chang'an Hall, and the offering and announcement rites were performed as in the ancestral temple, to await completion of the temple before transfer and enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that in the second year of Zhide, because the imperial ancestral temple was under repair, new spirit tablets were made and placed in Chang'an Hall, and the offering and announcement rites were performed as in the ancestral temple, to await completion of the temple before transfer and enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 當時議論，無所是非。

translations.literal: At that time in discussion there was no dispute.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in discussion there was no dispute.

sentences.zh: 竊知今者京城除大内正衙外，別無殿宇。

translations.literal: I know that at present in the capital, apart from the inner palace and main audience hall, there are no other halls.
translations.idiomatic: I know that at present in the capital, apart from the inner palace and main audience hall, there are no other halls.

sentences.zh: 伏聞先有詔旨，且以少府監大廳權充太廟。

translations.literal: I have heard there was already an edict temporarily using the great hall of the Palace Directorate as the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard there was already an edict temporarily using the great hall of the Palace Directorate as the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 伏縁十一室於五間之中，陳設隘狹，伏請接續廳之兩頭，成十一室，薦饗之。

translations.literal: Because eleven chambers within five bays are cramped for arrangement, I humbly request extending the two ends of the adjoining hall to form eleven chambers for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Because eleven chambers within five bays are cramped for arrangement, I humbly request extending the two ends of the adjoining hall to form eleven chambers for offerings.

sentences.zh: 三太后廟，即於監内西南，別取屋宇三間，且充廟室。

translations.literal: For the temple of the three empresses, take three rooms in the southwest of the directorate and temporarily use them as temple chambers.
translations.idiomatic: For the temple of the three empresses, take three rooms in the southwest of the directorate and temporarily use them as temple chambers.

sentences.zh: 候太廟修奉畢日，別議遷祔。」

translations.literal: When repair of the imperial ancestral temple is completed, transfer and enshrinement may be discussed separately."
translations.idiomatic: When repair of the imperial ancestral temple is completed, transfer and enshrinement may be discussed separately."

sentences.zh: 敕旨依奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其神主、法物、樂懸，皆盈孫奏重修制，知禮者稱爲博洽。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets, ritual objects, and musical instruments were all remade on Yingsun's memorial; those who understood ritual praised his breadth of learning.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets, ritual objects, and musical instruments were all remade on Yingsun's memorial; those who understood ritual praised his breadth of learning.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年十一月，昭宗郊祀圓丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Longji, Zhaozong performed the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Longji, Zhaozong performed the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 兩中尉楊復恭及兩樞密，皆請朝服。

translations.literal: Both army supervisors Yang Fugong and the two privy secretaries all requested court robes.
translations.idiomatic: Both army supervisors Yang Fugong and the two privy secretaries all requested court robes.

sentences.zh: 盈孫上疎曰：「臣昨赴齋宮，見中尉、樞密内臣，皆具朝服。

translations.literal: Yingsun submitted a memorial: "Yesterday when I went to the fasting palace I saw the army supervisors and privy secretaries, all inner officials, fully equipped in court robes.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun submitted a memorial, "Yesterday when I went to the fasting palace I saw the army supervisors and privy secretaries, all inner officials, fully equipped in court robes.

sentences.zh: 臣尋前代及國朝典令，無内官朝服制度。

translations.literal: I have examined former dynasties and our court's statutes and orders; there is no institution of court robes for inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined former dynasties and our court's statutes and orders; there is no institution of court robes for inner officials.

sentences.zh: 伏以皇帝陛下，承天御暦，聖祚中興，祗見宗祧，克陳大禮，皆稟髙祖、太宗之成制，必循虞、夏、商、周之舊經。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the emperor, receiving Heaven's mandate and governing the era, with the sacred reign in restoration, has reverently appeared before the ancestral temple and can perform the great rites—all following the completed institutions of Gaozu and Taizong, and necessarily following the old canons of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou.
