translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the emperor, receiving Heaven's mandate and governing the era, with the sacred reign in restoration, has reverently appeared before the ancestral temple and can perform the great rites—all following the completed institutions of Gaozu and Taizong, and necessarily following the old canons of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 軒冕服章，式遵彜憲。

translations.literal: Carriages, caps, robes, and insignia should follow canonical law.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages, caps, robes, and insignia should follow canonical law.

sentences.zh: 若内官要衣朝服，令依所守官本品之服。

translations.literal: If inner officials must wear court robes, let them wear the robes of the official rank they hold.
translations.idiomatic: If inner officials must wear court robes, let them wear the robes of the official rank they hold.

sentences.zh: 事雖無據，粗可行之。

translations.literal: Though the matter lacks precedent, it may roughly be done.
translations.idiomatic: Though the matter lacks precedent, it may roughly be done.

sentences.zh: 臣忝禮司，合具陳奏。」

translations.literal: I, who am charged with ritual affairs, should set it forth in full."
translations.idiomatic: I, who am charged with ritual affairs, should set it forth in full."

sentences.zh: 時中貴皆如宰相大臣朝服，故盈孫論之。

translations.literal: At that time the powerful inner officials all wore court robes like chancellors and great ministers; therefore Yingsun argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the powerful inner officials all wore court robes like chancellors and great ministers; therefore Yingsun argued against it.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，嘉其所守。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not follow it, he approved his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor did not follow it, he approved his integrity.

sentences.zh: 轉秘書少監，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 徐晦，進士擢第，登直言極諫制科，授櫟陽尉，皆自楊憑所薦。

translations.literal: Xu Hui passed the jinshi examination, passed the direct-criticism examination, and was appointed magistrate of Liyang—all through Yang Ping's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hui passed the jinshi examination, passed the direct-criticism examination, and was appointed magistrate of Liyang—all through Yang Ping's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 及憑得罪，貶臨賀尉，交親無敢祖送者；

translations.literal: When Ping was found guilty and demoted to magistrate of Linhe, relatives and friends none dared escort him on his way;
translations.idiomatic: When Ping was found guilty and demoted to magistrate of Linhe, none of his relatives and friends dared escort him on his way;

sentences.zh: 獨晦送至藍田，與憑言別。

translations.literal: only Hui escorted him as far as Lantian and spoke his farewell with Ping.
translations.idiomatic: only Hui escorted him as far as Lantian and spoke his farewell with Ping.

sentences.zh: 時故相權德輿與憑交分最深，知晦之行，因謂晦曰：「今日送臨賀，誠爲厚矣，無乃爲累乎！」

translations.literal: At that time the former chancellor Quan Deyu, who had the deepest ties with Ping, knowing of Hui's journey, therefore told Hui: "Today in escorting the Linhe magistrate you have indeed shown great depth—but will it not become a burden?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the former chancellor Quan Deyu, who had the deepest ties with Ping, knowing of Hui's journey, therefore told Hui, "Today in escorting the Linhe magistrate you have indeed shown great depth—but will it not become a burden?"

sentences.zh: 晦曰：「晦自布衣受楊公之眷，方茲流播，爭忍無言而別？

translations.literal: Hui replied: "Hui, from commoner status, received Lord Yang's favor; now that he is cast into exile, how could I bear to part without a word?
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "Hui, from commoner status, received Lord Yang's favor; now that he is cast into exile, how could I bear to part without a word?

sentences.zh: 如他日相公爲奸邪所譖，失意於外，晦安得與相公輕別？」

translations.literal: If someday, Lord Chancellor, you are slandered by the wicked and lose favor outside the capital, how could Hui lightly part from the Lord Chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: If someday, Lord Chancellor, you are slandered by the wicked and lose favor outside the capital, how could Hui lightly part from the Lord Chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 德輿嘉其眞懇，大稱之於朝。

translations.literal: Deyu admired his sincerity and praised him greatly at court.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu admired his sincerity and praised him greatly at court.

sentences.zh: 不數日，御史中丞李夷簡請爲監察，晦白夷簡曰：「生平不踐公門，公何取信而見獎拔？」

translations.literal: Within a few days Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian requested him as investigating censor; Hui told Yijian: "All my life I have not crossed the gates of great officials—why do you trust and reward me with promotion?"
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian requested him as investigating censor; Hui told Yijian, "All my life I have not crossed the gates of great officials—why do you trust and reward me with promotion?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「聞君送楊臨賀，不顧犯難，肯負國乎？」

translations.literal: Yijian replied: "I heard that you escorted Yang the Linhe magistrate, not fearing offense and willing to bear the state's burden—is that not so?"
translations.idiomatic: Yijian replied, "I heard that you escorted Yang the Linhe magistrate, not fearing offense and willing to bear the state's burden—is that not so?"

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became known.

sentences.zh: 歴殿中侍御史、尚書郎，出爲晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as attendant censor and director in the Secretariat, and went out as prefect of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as attendant censor and director in the Secretariat, and went out as prefect of Jin.

sentences.zh: 入拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 寶暦元年，出爲福建觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he went out as supervisory commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he went out as supervisory commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二年，入爲工部侍郎，出爲同州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered [the capital] as Vice Minister of Works, then went out as prefect of Tong and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he returned to the capital as Vice Minister of Works, then went out as prefect of Tong and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，征拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 五年，爲太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 晦性強直，不隨世態，當官守正。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was forceful and upright; he did not follow the ways of the age and in office upheld rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's nature was forceful and upright; he did not follow the ways of the age and in office upheld rectitude.

sentences.zh: 唯嗜酒太過，晩年喪明，乃至沈廢。

translations.literal: Only he loved wine too much; in his later years he lost his sight and was reduced to utter incapacity.
translations.idiomatic: Only he loved wine too much; in his later years he lost his sight and was reduced to utter incapacity.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 開成三年三月卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously given the title of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously honored as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：温、柳二公，以文行飾躬，砥礪名節，當官守法，侃侃有大臣之節，而竟不登三事，位止正卿。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: The two lords Wen and Liu, adorning themselves with literary conduct, honing their name and integrity, upholding the law in office, were earnest and possessed the integrity of great ministers—yet in the end they did not ascend to the Three Dukes and stopped at regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The two lords Wen and Liu, adorning themselves with literary conduct, honing their name and integrity, upholding the law in office, were earnest and possessed the integrity of great ministers—yet in the end they did not ascend to the Three Dukes and stopped at regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 所以知公輔之量，以和爲貴。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the measure of chief minister values harmony.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that the measure of chief minister values harmony.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝畏汲黯而相孫弘，太宗重魏徴而委玄齡，其旨遠也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han feared Ji An yet made Sun Hong chancellor; Taizong valued Wei Zheng yet entrusted Xuanling—how far-reaching the intent!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han feared Ji An yet made Sun Hong chancellor; Taizong valued Wei Zheng yet entrusted Xuanling—how far-reaching the intent!

sentences.zh: 韋、崔名士，薦賢致主，綽有古風。

translations.literal: Wei and Cui were famous scholars who recommended the worthy to serve the ruler; they had abundant ancient style.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Cui were famous scholars who recommended the worthy to serve the ruler; they had abundant ancient style.

sentences.zh: 殷司空治民，斯爲循吏，而忠規壯節，至晩不衰。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yin in governing the people was a model circumspect official, yet his loyal remonstrance and stalwart integrity did not fade even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yin in governing the people was a model circumspect official, yet his loyal remonstrance and stalwart integrity did not fade even in old age.

sentences.zh: 徐、郭讜言，郁爲佳士。

translations.literal: Xu and Guo's forthright words were rich and formed excellent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Guo's forthright words were rich and formed excellent scholars.

sentences.zh: 如數君者，實爲令人。

translations.literal: Men such as these several lords were truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as these several lords were truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：柳氏禮法，公忠節概。

translations.literal: Praise runs: The Liu family's ritual law, public loyalty and stalwart integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Praise runs: The Liu family's ritual law, public loyalty and stalwart integrity.

sentences.zh: 搏撃爲優，彌綸則隘。

translations.literal: Striking blows was their strength; weaving governance was their limit.
translations.idiomatic: Striking blows was their strength; weaving governance was their limit.

sentences.zh: 夏卿獎拔，晦叔匡將。

translations.literal: Xiaqing rewarded and elevated; Huishu supported and guided.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing rewarded and elevated; Huishu supported and guided.

sentences.zh: 徐、郭之議，金玉鏘鏘。

translations.literal: The remonstrance of Xu and Guo—gold and jade, ringing clear.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance of Xu and Guo—gold and jade, ringing clear.
